title: Landon Jackson: "I'm Really Excited About This Upcoming Year" | Buffalo Bills
text: Welcome back to One Bills Live. To finish off our show today, we're excited to be joined by Bill's defensive end, Landon Jackson, who joins us now. I mean, happened a lot throughout college. And then getting here throughout the draft prep and the uh like all the combine and senior bowl and all that, kind of made that decision to get lighter for that. Uh don't know if that was the best decision. don't know if it was not, but at the end of the day, at this point, I just feel like it it makes a lot more sense to really get that weight back on and play at a weight that I feel confident playing at. Uh allows me to play a lot more free when I'm not worried about if I can hold a double team at a certain being too light, this and that. So, uh I'm I'm really excited about this coming year and being able to play at the the weight that I feel comfortable playing at. >> Yeah. I know you said when you spoke to media last week that 285 is what you'd like to play at this season and it was fun to hear both you and Jim Leonard talk about you know the defensive jargon for this season like what you'll be playing in in this new 34 scheme feeling comfortable at 4i and then playing tight heavy five technique something that you did at Arkansas and Jim Leonard spoke about watching you in college and being really excited for what that's going to be in Buffalo's defense this season for fans who are like four eye five tech. So rather that be if I have to slide in and even play some nose or something, you know, be able to do that if I if guys go down and I have to move to outside backer for a game or something, just be able to do all of it. and I don't feel like I could play as much outside if I did get heavier and go into like the 300s, but then at the same time, I definitely couldn't play a heavy five or the four eye at 260, you know? So, I feel like uh this game fits me great, you know? It's it's what I excelled at in college, what got me to this point. So, uh basically I just feel like if it if it wasn't broke, don't try to change it, you know? So, basically just get that weight back to where where it was in college. >> Yeah. You said that you played this way, you played in this defensive scheme in college at Arkansas, then you kind of took a year where you were in a different scheme last year, your rookie year here in Buffalo. Now you're back into it. Has it started to >> Has it started to feel like old hat? I mean, are you are you starting to see, oh yeah, okay, I I you know, is that is that starting to happen? >> Yeah, we haven't got uh pads on yet or anything, but just from uh walkthroughs and then our uh OTAAS and everything definitely feeling a lot more powerful. Definitely feeling back to how I felt in college, like real comfortable in this game. So, uh, overall, I feel like it's going to be a much better year for me. I feel like it's I'm really going to excel in this defense and really excited to see where it goes. >> I mean, how exciting for a young player like yourself last season doesn't go how you wanted it to due to injuries. You playing just a few games. You get in this new defense, new head coach comes in, new defensive coordinator, and you learn, man, we're switching to this defense that I thrive in, and I can't wait to see what it looks like. I can't wait to see um what the defense as a whole looks like once you guys get into it, really when the season begins in September. When you think about Buffalo's defense under Jim Leonard, what are a few words that describe what what you guys are going to be doing? >> In my opinion, aggressive for sure. I feel like we're going to get after the quarterback. Uh let our our really talented DBs get cover back there. Uh and I mean get after the quarterback. We're going to biggest change in this defense. Uh we're definitely going to have to we're definitely going to stop the run a lot better than we did in previous years. Uh I feel like that's probably the biggest thing we're making an emphasis on right now is being able to stop the run and be uh be the top team in the league at stopping the run. So, that's probably the biggest thing that I've I'm really focusing on is being able to dominate the run and then whenever it's time to get after the quarterback, get back there. >> Well, I know congratulations are in order. I know you you came in, you were drafted and you were married and then you shared uh just last week that you and your wife uh welcomed your first baby April 3rd. Uh what are the details here? What do we need to know? >> Man, it's been great. You know, uh she she's been sleeping good. Everything's been going good, you know. So, uh, wife's been doing great at home with her and everything, taking care of her. And I mean, it's it's all a blessing. >> Give me an idea because I unlike you, I'm I being married gives you a little bit more of of a tethered off the- field life. You're a little bit more foundational, a little bit slower pace. Uh, the baby certainly changes things. Give me an idea of how you feel. Um because I'm sure you do feeling that having your wife with you uh having the new baby is more is probably helpful for your football career >> um slowing your off the- field responsibilities down. Having that priority aside from football gives you a little bit >> more of a calm base to to build your foundation for your career on. Give us an idea. Share with us your thoughts about having a family now uh as such a young player in the NFL. Yeah, really. Uh, biggest thing is, uh, man, it it it makes you want to go hard for them. You're playing for something more than yourself. And, uh, at the end of the day, everything I'm doing here is to be able to provide for my daughter and my wife and, uh, be able to be the best husband possible. And I feel like I'm selling my family short if I come in here and I'm slacking off or I'm not giving giving my all. So, that's probably the biggest thing that it it changes. Uh, it just, in my opinion, makes you go harder. I mean, and not saying guys who don't have that aren't going hard, but it's something you don't it's a feeling you don't really know until you you're in that situation. So, it I I know I got a little girl relying on me and my wife relying on me. So, makes me go 10 times harder and just uh make sure I'm going to give this thing all I got. >> Landon, we're so happy for you and we're so excited that you're back in uniform feeling healthy and ready to go in this defense. We're both cheering for you and I I I really can't wait to watch you this season. Thank you. Thank

title: QB Gardner Minshew OTA Press Conference | Arizona Cardinals 2026
text: How do you feel like things are going in terms [clears throat] of the install and where you guys are at offensively? Uh it's been great. And that helps a lot, you know? Cuz there's times when yeah, it is against the odds, but man, I've been so fortunate and then I wouldn't trade any of it. I've learned so much and I really feel like it's prepared me to be where I am now. Do you do you feel like you're still trying to just prove yourself in this league? >> Uh man, always. I'm always trying to get better, always trying to learn. Um at the end of the day, I want to be a quarterback that wins in this league. Want to win at a high level, play at a high level. Um I think that's everybody's uh you know, goal as a quarterback and uh I'm excited to be here with an opportunity and a great group of guys around me. You've started, you've been a backup, you've been a lot of places like people have said. How do you You seem like a guy that kind of thrives on uncertainty and you're kind of in a another situation here where there's an opportunity, but there's also, you know, uncertainty. How How do you deal with that? How have you been so good at that during your career? Yeah, fortunately I've had a lot of experience, you know, kind of in all those roles, you know, whether it's back to, you know, college, pros. Um at the end of the day all you really have is the work that you put in. You know, at some point somebody's going to be better than you and they're going to play. At some point you'll be the best guy in the room, you'll get a chance to play. Uh all you really have is your opportunity to work and get better and to enjoy it with the guys around you and that's what it's been a blast so far working with this staff, working with these guys on the team and I look forward to just continuing that. LaFleur told an anecdote about when you were in the All-Star game in college and you called him up and and did that the hours of What made you want to give him a call and get ahead like that and did that give you some kind of of bond with with Mike LaFleur at that point? So, like building those relationships, showing uh you know, whoever it is these coaches that you do care, that you want to do it right. I remember going into the Senior Bowl, uh I was like a late round projection, you know, but I had an opportunity there and I was going to make the most of it. So, I ended up uh I knew Nick Mullens, you know, who's in San Fran. I reached out to him. I was like, "Hey, do you know anybody on staff? How can I, you know, get some offense?" A lot has been made about your RV. What's the what's the setup like man? Oh man, it's got four wheels and a bed do you ready to go. >> [laughter] >> What's the what's one of the best road trips you've been on? Oh man, um I don't know man they're all they're all good in their own way. I've spent some time out here in Sedona, Flagstaff, Grand Canyon. Uh I'd like to try to get out to like Greer and do some like fly fishing out there. I think that sounds pretty cool. Uh but now there's so much out here it's it's really cool. How do you see your role as the as the veteran in that quarterback room especially with the rookie in Carson back and and if you were Carson what sort of questions would you ask of a veteran in the room? Yeah I think the first thing you know is your responsibility to be the great example, you know, to do things the right way, to come in prepared, to lead your guys, lead your huddle. Uh I think that's you know as a young guy that's the best thing you can have as a good example to watch and see how it's done. Uh so trying to do that for them, answering any questions they have, um you know, trying to just help give any tips or anything that I see with them. Uh they're great dudes, been learning, uh just trying to soak up anything they can. Uh so it's been a lot of fun working with that quarterback room. You've shared an offensive meeting room with one of the best tight ends last year in Travis Kelce. What makes Trey McBride potentially on that trajectory to be kind of that next up and comer tight end? No Trey is so good man. It's it's been really cool being around him, seeing you know, obviously all the success he had last year but seeing it first hand how competitive is he is every day, how much um man his change of direction in and out of breaks, his football IQ, understanding zone, how to win in man. Uh he's awesome, man. And really, you know, all you can ask for in a in a tight end. And I think he's set up in this offense to be really productive. Of all the of all the offenses they've played in, which is closest to what you're doing here now? Um man, I don't know. In a weird way, like the air raid back in college, because this is the reason this does so well is it thrives off complimentary looks and simplicity with the illusion of complexity through motions, similar formations. We really don't do a ton off each look, but just enough to put a seed of doubt. And the idea is that we're going to get really good at what we do. Um so that's been a blast getting in this offense. I think it gives the players a ton of confidence when hey, we have these things. This is what we're going to do. It's your job to make it come come to life. And I think we got the guys to do that. Was the scheme of this offense a big reason why coming here was appealing to you? Oh, it's huge. Yeah. No, seeing what coach La Fleur's done, um and what they've been able to do in San >> [snorts] >> with the Rams these last couple years, like man, it's been one of my favorite teams to watch on tape. Uh they've obviously been had been super successful. Uh so I was fired up to come here and see the guys that they had. Um I think there's a lot of talent uh on that offensive side. You seem pretty fired up when you're out there on the practice field with the offense going and moving, getting first downs, meetings. Is that just a natural part of who you are? I guess, man. It's fun to play football, you know? I think we forget that sometimes. Um and it gets hard and it's tough work sometimes, but man, it's awesome to be out here, to be, you know, 30 years old, my eighth year in the NFL, like being able to play ball, like dude, it doesn't get any better. Is the expectation right now that you are competing to be considered for the starting job? Uh I don't know, man. I'm getting the reps I'm getting right now, trying to do the best I can, trying to help our team. >> Mhm.

Uh, you know, just trying to, you know, telling these guys be where your feet are and improve, you know, one day at a time, and so you just try to remind yourself that as well. Obviously, in this seat, money seat, whatever, you always have to plan for for whatever it is, roster, schedules, and all those kind of things, but um, to even think about next week's OTAs is hard. Like, I'm one of that I can't get scripted in until I see this practice see what our guys need to improve on, what we did well, what routes we can work off of, different stuff. So, um, you know, again, just trying to be where your feet are. Do you feel at peace in terms of implementation and all that stuff, where you want it to be at this point? Yeah, actually, truthfully, I think we're we're probably a little bit further than I would think. Um, and I and I would say the reason for that is we got a very veteran team, you know, uh, 70 or so, you know, in the in the low 70s, those guys have played football, you know, whether they've played on Sundays, but they've been a part of camps and stuff like that. So, the implementation of it, one, they were here through phase one, and so not only are your {quote} {unquote} ones or whatever, um, you know, going to be up to speed, but your next groups are, because again, they've they've been hearing it. So, um, I'm I'm pleased, I guess you could say schematically with where they're at and in their knowledge of it. Now, it's just, again, never getting bored of doing the same reps over and over and over and hitting the same blocks and running the same routes and doing your same hook drops and working your man techniques and working your same rush lanes and all that, and that's uh, you know, what we got to focus on. Were there any things that kind of jumped out week one that your guys impressed you with? Um, kind of what I was just saying, you know, in terms of I I I thought, particularly from practice one to practice two. Now, this ended up being practice five right here, but I thought every single day, you know, and I've I've said it, I don't want to be a broken record, but I believe it. I thought our operation on both sides has just gotten better and better, you know. Um, first day from a defensive line uh, perspective, uh, cleats weren't getting in the dirt, hand weren't getting in the dirt fast enough as we were going up there and snapping it, you know, on our quick count. Second day, I thought that improved and it's only gotten better and better, you know, so um I've liked the way that these guys have again lined up, communicated, done all that. Um still got a long way to go in terms of just banking all these reps because uh there's a lot of reps to be had. You talked for about your first interaction with Gardner back at the Senior Bowl, I believe it was. Um how is he different now that you're having a chance to interact with him all the time now compared to maybe that week back in the day? That's a good question cuz I don't know how different he is, you know, it what you see from him every single day is is his love for the game and and um love for the locker room, love for just just football in general and that's that's what you felt, you know, like I've said on that story um when he wanted to meet on that that senior uh you know, senior um Senior Bowl playbook, I should say. Uh and I didn't know if it was going to be 20 minutes and I had to finally tell my wife uh cancel our dinner plans cuz he's going to he's going to go for about 4 hours and it was great, you know, so um he's still in that same mindset, he loves it. Um only thing different is is, you know, hair might be frolicking a little bit more and he's a dad. >> [snorts] >> Is he somebody that kind of personality and it's kind of been well chronicled the kind of personality has, is that something good in a locker room to have somebody like that? I think what's good in the locker room is just authentically being yourself, you know, um so whether that's coaches or players, just you just be you and and guys are going to respect guys that are just being themselves as long as they're going to work and putting their best foot forward every day, so um Gardner's very uh confident and comfortable with who he is just like a ton of our guys are and that's, you know, that's really all you want out of out of people in that locker room and people in general. Coach, a handful of guys not out here this week. Is that concerning at all for you? Uh no, I mean the the the few guys that that weren't out there that you guys probably saw today, um you know, very much we knew, you know, that they were going to be here and a lot of it was planned ahead. I mean, shoot, I don't want to put it out there, but one of them just, you know, had a baby, stuff like that. So, um, you know, good for him. Is uh how's Paris doing? Is he Does Yeah, Paris is now That's one right there that we knew well ahead that this was going to be a day. Uh, Paris is absolutely fine. Coach, with with Marvin, now that you've had a handful of practices with him, what has stood out to you about his uh his process? Yeah, that he goes about it the same way every single day, you know, he's um he attacks it in the meeting room. He's a he's a really smart dude. Like football, it's like he kind of grew up in football, you know? So, like football makes sense to him. Um, like it's almost one of those things and it doesn't bother me, but it's like, are you bored in this meeting right now? Which is a good thing, you know, the guys that it just makes sense. It's like they don't need to hear it three, four, five times. Some guys do and that's okay. I mean, that's part of the the process right there. Um, so for him it's just again getting out there every single day working on his craft. I love watching uh him, Michael, and some of the DBs after practice. They're just working releases, you know, they don't even have a ball out there. Then they'll go to the jugs and and go about, you know, go about that process. So, uh he's just consistent in terms of how what his approach is and uh you know, looking to improve every day. Since you grew up in football yourself, can you relate to a guy like that any differently than other players? And is it are the conversations any different because you guys have that long history in the game? I mean, I think maybe in some aspects we can relate to it cuz we are around it. You know, obviously him and I have a different skill set. Uh and uh his his pops and my dad had a different skill set as well. So, I think there's probably a different relatable in terms of, you know, just football and sports in general, but uh you know, again, you grew up around the game, grew up around like some of my favorite memories were just when my dad would have the DBs over from Central Michigan and you're just having dinner or whatnot and you're just getting to hang around them. And again, those were those were my superheroes, you know, all of them. And um none of them played in the NFL, but at the time what what did I care, you know? And I'm sure Marv probably felt the same way growing up being around the locker room and and all that. And you know, naturally, whether it's football or other sports, you just kind of kind of understand it sometimes a little bit more. With the amount of information Jacoby's missing by not being here, how tough is that for you to to know that when he does come back, if he comes back, you know, how much he has to catch up on? Yeah, like I said, I mean, you'd be hard-pressed to see if Jacoby hasn't done most of what we've uh are doing physically, [snorts] you know? And so, it's just kind of it's word association from that point and cadences and all that kind of stuff. But the hardest thing to teach a player is the speed of the game in NFL game in general. And he's played a lot of ball, so he'll be just fine. Is it a concern to you that Josh Sweat is here? Uh, it's not, no. Are you guys open to trading him if those offers come in? Uh, you know, I don't even read into the offers. I don't look at them. I'm just excited of the fact that I don't have to game plan against this guy. Uh, I got to know him when I first got this job. Um, he's a good dude. He goes about his process, you know, and he's not the the first guy to go about his process the way he is in terms of how he's training and all that. I've been around a lot of really good football players that have done this. Um, but uh like I said, I'm just I'm happy I don't have to game plan against him. Is there any kind of positive with the quarterback room with Jacoby not being here creating opportunities for other guys, whether it's in the classroom or on the Yeah, you know, I yeah, you could spin it that way, you know, anytime you have um name that position and and guys get more reps, it it's a positive for them, you know? So, um anytime that uh they're stepping on the field, they're they're they're learning, you know, whether it's a good play, bad play, or somewhere in between. The ability to just be out there, like again, the the the meeting room, showing all the clips of all the different teams we've been a part and how we're building this thing, both offense, defense, special teams, it's all great. You got to go out and do it, and that's why, you know, like the you want to get good at football, you got to go play football. You got to practice, like no crap, right? And uh so, um you know, anytime those guys at any position can get more opportunities, it's going to be better for them, yes. With Gardner now that you have the field of him, how does his How have you seen his skills that kind of translate into what you want to do offensively? Yeah, I mean, I've you know, again, he's played a lot of football and and and had the opportunity to see him to see him firsthand, you know, whether it be playing him or, you know, obviously through the film and all that. So, again, he knows the game. He's been around a lot of different systems. He's been asked to do a lot. I mean, you you think about what we're doing compared to let's just say Philly when he was there and and backing up Jalen Hurts and then Jalen goes down and he's running that system, you know? And so, he's been a part of all this. Again, very similar in terms of just figuring out what the words were, really. He had done something like most of what our scheme is asking him to do. And now, again, it's just getting used to it, the guys that he's throwing to, getting used to the line, getting used to Fro, and kind of that huddle and and Jalen. It's been about almost 5 weeks now since the draft. How have you seen Carson back kind of develop into this offense and into this comfort level here and and where is he at right now? Yeah, it's kind of it's in that same vein, you know, I do think the game makes sense to Carson. I think he's done an awesome job. I think Matt Shawb and Nathaniel Hackett have done an incredible job with him in terms of just teaching him the foundations of of the West Coast system, whatever that means. But really, that means just decision-making, timing, and then accuracy with it. But I mean, that that's kind of a prerequisite level that you got to have, you know, when when you end up coming in. But, you know, understanding what our reads are, understanding what the timing and the footwork is, and and how it's all, you know, kind of tied together. That makes sense to Carson. Again, I give a lot of credit to those guys, but but, you know, like I said, I think all three of those guys have done a great job and Carson's putting in the time to understand what we're asking from him. You spoke the way you would like some ways that you want to slow roll a little bit the integration of the rookie class into into the rest of the team. I guess how would you kind of describe your philosophy with rookies and how you bring them up to speed with the rest of >> Yeah, it's a good question and and typically I'd I'd 100% agree with you, but typically you have quite a few more rookies than this, you know, and and so naturally when you're around other guys like a rookie's around a lot of guys that have been around the system phase one, whatever, but have played football. they know what they're doing, they know what kind of we're asking from them, so they they just naturally kind of pick up on what other guys are doing, you know, so if that makes sense. Um you know, I I've always said that the rookie will be ready when the rookie's ready. With that being said, this league doesn't wait around, so there's a level of urgency that everyone's got to have coaching them to the guy receiving the information and going out and doing what we're asking them to do. Um if you don't, then it's just going to catch up with you and the show goes on and the league just goes on, you know, so um there there there is a a certain level of patience you got to have knowing that everyone's going to be different and and that's not just the rookies, that's all the guys learning the system. Uh but but that really is a thing, but always going back to hey, we got to go, all right, there's an urgency uh to this. With with Gardner and Keaton getting most of the snaps, the vast majority of snaps today that we saw, where how does Carson work his way into that rotation? Yeah, Carson Carson's been he's been going, he's been getting just as many reps as as everyone else. Um so that was just a a little something today that's uh you know, he'll be he'll be ready to roll. How much [snorts] growth have you seen from Jeremiah in the last couple weeks just sitting in the practice field and getting acclimated? Yeah, just uh you know, it's a running back in shorts, let's be real, you know, so like even I mean that's the first thing that comes to my head. These these running backs, you just want them to understand one, the protection scheme because it is a little bit different than say what he was doing at Notre Dame. That's just NFL pressures and stuff in in general, right? And so um you know, yeah, you can get that in practice particularly with what our defense does, but but that's going to come throughout training camp, having those joints against Green Bay, obviously getting into the preseason games and all that. And two, when we actually put the pads on, and and we're actually running the football, hitting the blocks with the pads. Like I think we're doing as good as we can in terms of getting the run game in, but but this is mostly a passing camp. And that's just kind of what this league has turned into, right, wrong, or indifferent, but the rules are the rules. You know, but I have liked the way that we have been able to run, you know, the ball a little bit in terms of you know, the offense and defense line working with each other, the second levels not making it where it's a car wreck every single time, cuz you can't do that anymore. So, running backs, you'll get a better feel, I know I long-winded on that one, but you'll get a better feel when you get the pads on, but he's doing a good job. Where you're at schematically, how much more does do you feel like you can put on guys' plates as the week keep going? Well, I and that's why, you know, I don't have a Friday script yet, because you you always want to reevaluate after every practice in my opinion. You know, you got a plan, but plans change based on man, they really did a great job with that. We got to give, you know, some complimentary cuts off that or complimentary plays, or you can see they're overloaded. And and that's a daily process, and that's part of us as coaches. Like again, you have plans, but we got to put them in the best position every single day to go have the most successful practice they can. Um sometimes we're going to have some plays that on purpose we're putting them in those, you know, situations to see how they handle that. So, it's not always spoon-fed to them, you know, so day-to-day thing, and that's that's kind of one of my favorite parts about OTAs and training camp is yeah, you got a plan, but plans change.

title: Jeff Ulbrich, Bill Callahan, & Robert Prince talk player development during OTAs | Press Conference
text: kind of hard or rare to find like really good alignment, right, between like a coach and GM. You feel like you've seen that here with this regime? >> Yeah, absolutely. Like the the relationship I think that Ian Kevin has is um it's tremendous. There's there's respect. Um there's a level of uh you can see them just playing off each other and making decisions in regard to to free agency, the draft, and everything in between. So, um it's one of those rare occurrences that that exists here. what about it or I guess how have they approached it when they initially got here. Could you tell how early on could you tell that this is a regime that really can find alignment and has reached alignment? >> It just all the questions they were asking, you know, whenever there's like that's the the start of the conversation. I think you got a chance to be to be special and and build it the right way. You know, when when you come in just dictating, I think sometimes things can get a little wonky, but um it wasn't that way at all. And uh and I've enjoyed it. Like it's been a great environment and uh and I'm learning a lot, too. So >> you're having to you're having to replace two very valuable players from your defense last year with Onyada and then Kate Ellis. What have you what are your early impressions from those units just in the wake of those guys losing those guys and and the guys who have since come in and filled in? >> Yeah, both tremendous players and even better people as you guys know. Um going to be hard to replace on the field, off the field and and everywhere in between. So um we miss them, you know, we love them, respected what they did here and and they're going to do amazing things in their new spots. uh and they they won't be replaced by by necessarily um one person, you know, it's going to be a little bit by committee. You know, both of them had a really unique skill set and u but I do believe we have the guys in the building to get it done. You know, it's it's going to be a lot of work and and we're going to try to have to figure things out through through the spring and training camp and and uh but I'm excited about the guys we have here. >> What is your vision for Mason Smith, too? And and what does he offer that I don't want necessarily what that R doesn't, but like what is the difference there in their games? Um I would you mind if I just talk on Mason? Yeah. Because I and and I really appreciate Rook and all he did and he worked his butt off here and nothing but respect for him and wish him well with Jacksonville. Uh but Mason's just been a um a really pleasant surprise cuz you just don't know. You know, I know what he was in in in college and I was excited about that player and prospect, but until you get your hands on him, it's it's just unfamiliar territory. But uh you know since he stepped in this building he's just showed eagerness to learn um intent to work uh great attitude. He's enormous you know he's a big guy with uh incredible movement for the for the size of man that he is you know so whenever you got a big guy like that that can move that that has real intent that that loves this game willing to put the work in like something special usually occurs. So I'm excited about his future here. What's the next step for Jaylen Walker and what do you think uh the potential and growth can be in year two? I >> there's a lot of steps. You know, the the fact that he is so versatile, the fact that like his calling card is his his ability to do so many different things. Um >> we're going to make we're going to we're going to need to to become better at everything that he does, whether it's the pass rush, edetting for the line of scrimmage, um small roll off the ball, uh coverage, blitz, um you know, like we're going to ask him to do a lot. He is one of those guys that's going to be in a similar role that Kaden had last year. And you know what we asked Kaden to do. I'd never been around anything like that before in the past. Just his I mean there was a days where he was an outside backer, days he was a defensive end, days he was an inside backer, days he was really in some ways a nickel, you know. So, um that's hard to replace. Uh Jaylen's up to the task and Jaylen's going to bring his own flavor to it, too. You know, I think Jaylen's got some some superpowers that are really unique and um he's he's tough. He loves this game. Um you know, he has this obvious skill set that we all see. What you don't see is the guy behind the scenes. He's got some real authentic leadership to him. A guy that's, you know, this this this word comes, you know, thrown around way too often, the force multiplier. But that's what he is. He's a guy that elevates people around him. And um he'll make us better collectively as he gets better individually. Jeff, when it comes to uh your pass rush, how much does the game planning change when you have James Spears in the lineup as opposed to have him out of the lineup? >> Uh we'll see how this group, you know, progresses and and comes together and and we'll see what we're capable of doing, you know, like when your rush is humming with four, you know, we'd all like to lean on that, you know, and play coverage and and um and obviously, you know, towards especially towards the end of the year, James got got going and and he really started to get a feel for it. So, you know, we'll see if we got a guy here that can replace that role, which um I'm excited about the guys that we have, whether it be Samson or or Brilen. It just there's countless guys with Ziz um uh all these guys just to see what they can do collectively and see see what they can do within this system. It's going to be exciting. >> So, you don't think you have to change anything? Just if he's in if he's not there, you can keep the same approach that you've had. >> Yeah. It ultimately it comes down to like this year's guys and the collective unit. You know, if if we can find four that can provide pass rush without blitzing, like that's where we're going to lean. You know, if um they need me to get them going at times, you know, with little help in regard to to pressure, then we're we're going to go down that road. You know, I think the beauty of what we built last year is we got the ability now to kind of go both ways, you know, so we can really fine-tune this thing based upon um the guys that we got out there. What do you envision for Avon Terrell? >> Um, I I've been blown away by his approach. Like, he's not he does not feel like the typical rookie. Like, he has a a rare maturity. You can tell his brother's had a lot of influence on him. Um, as we all know, AJ is just not only like one of the best corners in the world. Um, but just his approach is so, and this is not a shot at DBs, but it's just so not DB like, you know. Um, he he's his approach, his his demeanor is very linebacker-ish, you know, like the toughness that he demonstrates and and that he walks around, the way he carries himself is so unique, and you can definitely feel that on his brother. um excited about his future. Where his future is, I I couldn't tell you yet and I don't want to jump to conclusions and I don't want to put him somewhere where he can't necessarily thrive. So, um a lot of that will be figured out through spring and probably won't be really finalized through through training camp, you know, cuz he's another guy with versatility. I think he's got the ability to play inside and outside and um so a lot of that will be based upon competition and and kind of where he where it all works itself out and uh and then fit him best where where he can um contribute this year cuz I think I think he's going to be a guy that's going to be a significant contributor year one >> try look he looks excellent you know I've been excited for him um he's a guy that just he's one of those guys that loves the game so much and when he's when he's not out there he's hurt like it weighs so heavily on him, you know. So, um I'm so excited for him to finally get an opportunity to demonstrate who he is as a player and and uh the the thing I love about Brillin is like we talk about and and I know I talk at Nauseian about hard fist, but he's a guy that lives that, you know, strain, toughness, um high level process and execution and everything in between. So, I'm um I'm excited for us and probably more importantly for him to get out here and really show um the world and probably more importantly himself who he is as a football player. >> Going back to Jaylen, I remember you talking last year about you really wanting to master that that edge position. Um what did you how did you observe him be able to do that and then just to kind of add on to what you kind of mentioned about playing more of a Kaden Ellis role. Seems like more ability for him this year to stand up a little bit and be a little bit more versatile. >> Yeah. And I I put a lot of that on me that the fact that we didn't necessarily um take him where I where I think we could have taken him, you know, and and part of that was the emergence of Kaden. Part of that was the the the scheme was like it was going right and left and up and down and it was evolving and growing as the year went along. Um really exciting to see what it became by the last, you know, three or four games. And I thought, um, now there was some growing pains within that. And within that, like we didn't necessarily maybe feature him as well as we could have or develop him as well as we could have. So, I'm excited this year. Just such a clear vision for for what he'll do for us and and ways that we need to get him better and ways that he will get better. So, um I'm excited about what he'll become this year. >> How do you kind of manage the unknown? Like when when it comes to James Pierce, like no one knows what it's going to be. So, do you just act like he's not here anymore and there's a potential he comes back? I mean, how do you coach a real matter? How do you deal with that? I in all honesty and it and it's whether a guy gets fined or hurt, there's so many things that are always in play at this level. So, it's just the guys that are here today, the guys that we're going to we're going to ride with and and and develop and feature in the right ways and and uh you know, and you know, I I know that coach addressed that this morning. So, like you know, collecting information. We don't know exactly where that is yet, but you know, we're just going to coach the the guys that we have as best we can, feature them best we can, and and we'll go from there. Uh, I'm sorry if you've been asked this already, but Kevin was talking earlier about kind of just like the calming presence that Divine has just with other guys on the team. I'm curious whether it be when you're playing or coaching who in maybe role you kind of looked to or saw had that calming presence that exemplified that. >> Yeah. Gosh, he's so unique cuz I've been around like guys that are really demonstrative leaders that that can have that effect where it's like their voice just calms you down because they have such, you know, they're so demonstrative and so certain in everything they do and um and so even killed when it comes to whatever the situation it may be. They just they're that rock, you know, that you can lean on. And he does that in in a way I've never seen before. It's so unique in in his calmness and his demeanor and his consistency in all that he does. Um, I'm excited for him to get the green dot. I think it's going to be an opportunity to really push him in the direction that that he's headed. I think he's got the capacity to be an amazing leader, you know, and in a leader in his own unique way now, but um, an amazing leader and I think we saw just the tip of the iceberg from a player's perspective, what he can become. Um, so excited like, you know, he misses a few days here and there and this is no shot at anybody else. This is more a testament to him. when he's out there, we feel different. Like when when he's out there today, it was like like I feel calm, you know, it's just this big avatar out there, you know, you know, protecting big windows and he's just so, you know, so athletic and he's so intelligent and he's so instinctual and he's so long and big and and you know, he checks so many boxes for you, you know, and now to see him finally get this opportunity to to be the voice of the defense because I think he's ready for that and I'm excited for him in that way. He said that when we were talking to him earlier, he was like, "I'm not much of a talker." And he he is he's very like introvert is not the right word, but he's, you know, more of a quiet leader type of guy. Um, and he said something that you challenged him with was to be more vocal. Um, >> can you kind of walk me through kind of what that expectation is for him now in the role that you have him for? >> Yeah, he's Well, for one, when you get the green dot, you naturally have a stage with the defense because you're the voice and you're the one calling the defenses. you're the one making the checks and obviously you're getting help from the safeties and and the other linebackers, but um the stage is there for him. Now, now like I I always I'm careful about this cuz I don't I think disingenuine leaders, leaders that try to lead like someone else or someone that they're not, they will not be followed, you know, they won't be the force multiplier that we talk about. Um, so it's really finding his voice that's authentic to him, you know, and that's that's what's so um unique about him because you're right, he's not the big loud demonstrative pound my chest um constantly be in front of the group, but I think he has so much to say and he has so much value um in that way. I want to keep pushing him to speak and affect people because he can in such a an amazing positive way. And then some of the guys, other guys in that room like Christian Harris, Kindle Daniels, what have you seen from those guys and and kind of how do they support having a guy like that in the middle? >> Yeah, all of them. It's just they're a little, you know, a little silo of a family within our defense, that linebacker group. Um, already have amazing chemistry and you can see them intense competition in that group. like whoever ends up being the starter is going to have to earn it cuz there's a lot of talent in that room and whoever is the backup better be ready to play cuz I think there's going to be a role that they all deserve to have in some capacity. So, um I just think it's it's amazing group like in and that's the lineback group, but that's really the defense. Like it's it's that rare occurrence and I kind of spoke on this last year and I feel like we've gotten even better in this way that in this world that we live in that it's so about selfishness and self-promotion and about me rather than we and the team. Um we don't have that here. You know, you can't be an on this defense. You can't you can't be a self-promoter. you can't be if you do, you're going to stick out, you know, and and you're not going to be accepted and you're not going to you're not going to be a part of it very long. So, it's so refreshing for me to be able to come to a work space like this and get to coach guys that that want to be coached and developed and pushed and and that have such humility and and have so much grace and and kindness for each other. And that sounds really weird when you speak about football, but it but it lives here and it's going to be a big reason that that we're probably going to be better than than most think we'll be. What were some of your takeaways at the coach's clinic that you were able to go to? And is being a head coach one day still something that you would like to do? >> I I think it is, you know, I do um it'd be an exciting opportunity and I think I've been in this so long playing coaching and that I would love the challenge of um of doing that. You know, at the same time, like this has been an amazing experience for me this year cuz, you know, I've been with a lot of people that I kind of came up with, whether playing or coaching with Dan and Raheem and and even coach Carol and and all these guys that have had amazing influences on me, but they do come from a similar tree, you know, and to be with Kevin now, it's been awesome because I'm learning such a unique and different way. Not better, worse, just a different way. and it's helping me grow and it's pushing me to be maybe a little uncomfortable at times but in in the most best of ways. So, um yeah, I'm in my feet right now and like I said, I just I love coaching this group of guys and and I love this coaching staff that we have from top to bottom. It's just rare that you have all of that in one place. Usually there's I'm sure you guys all experience that in your workplaces. There's that one person you don't want to be around, you know, and and we don't have that here, you know, and I feel very fortunate that that is the case. Thank you. >> What do you like about Kendall Daniels when you talk about a guy who's converted safety now? He's kind of just a Swiss Army knife kind of kind of go everywhere. >> Yeah, we'll see. You know, I'm excited. I mean, he's he's obviously very young, inexperienced, and and um still fairly new to the linebacker position. Another guy like Deine who's a converted guy that was a safety at Oklahoma State and and even when he went to Oklahoma, do a little bit of everything. He played in the half field like a safety would. Then he'd play at the line of scrimmage, then he'd play off like so. Um, it's going to be it's going to be fun developing him and really seeing where he fits and where he can contribute year one. Um, I would I would say like and this is not just from an appearance standpoint because I get they're both long and tall and and ex safeties, but him and Divine are very similar in a lot of ways, you know, and and you couldn't ask for a better mentor in every way than Divine for Kendall and and Kendall success, a lot of it will be attributed to to being around Divine. So, it's going to be an awesome relationship as I see it grow and push each other and develop each other. >> You you you've seen a lot of great safety combinations in your day. How would you compare this starting group of safeties with some of the past? It looks like you guys are kind of going something special here. >> Yeah, it's it's as good as I've ever been around. And to think like X we know is going to be, you know, he's going to be a star and Jesse we know is a solidified star in this league. But I think both have such space to still grow and I know that X obviously like he's going to grow and get better. But I think even Jesse does too and and that's a byproduct of a guy that's just got amazing humility. Here's a guy that's been the face of the NFL as far as safety play is concerned for for quite a while now that's still so hungry to learn and grow and and such humility to help others around him. and and we've got some young guys in the room too that um and with the addition of Sydney Brown like it's it it we got some millionaire problems on the back end like trying to figure out you know how to utilize all these guys and how to feature these guys cuz I think there's so many guys on our back end whether it be safety nickel or corner that that deserve the right to be a part of what we're trying to build here. So it's going to be a it's going to be a good challenge for me. >> What have you seen from the guys uh that you've inherited here at Atlanta? How have they adopted adapted I guess you could say to your scheme? >> Uh It's been great. Well, you know, it's it's give and take and it's been fun. It's it's a great group of guys. Um and Coach Le did a phenomenal job here. You know, when he was here, he got you he's got this he's got the line rolling. You know, they're physical. They have a great attitude about themselves. They did a a great job producing in the run game. Uh so, I'm just here to maintain what they've done and improve upon it. Do you have a different approach when you come into a room where you've got a lot of veteran guys versus maybe younger guys? Does your approach change or do you come in and just do it the same way you would? >> Well, I think everybody's different. You know, I treat them all different. You know, I I I think uh you know, a 13-year vet like Jake versus a rookie walking in the door. >> Excuse me. >> Um I monitor that. I'm really careful about, you know, what I say to each person, you know, so I I want to confuse the young guys so I don't give them too much, but I also want to be able to, you know, challenge the older vets with some new information, maybe things that they haven't heard or things that they haven't done before. >> We were talking to Jake about how he you kind of dropped some references like, oh, when I taught Joe Thomas this or this and this, and he's like, some of that might go over some of the younger guys head, but I have a big appreciation for it. Is there some of that for you you're like, "Oh, this you might know not who know who that is." Like think of that when you talk to the younger guys. >> I do. I'm I'm cognizant of that and uh because of the generational gap. So, I just make them do rookie reports, you know. I make them do a little bit more, you know, uh, background because I have such a great reverence for the game and and and I think the history of the game is important, you know, and it's important for the rookies to understand, you know, the NFL and, you know, we we stand on the broad shoulders for the guys that have come before us. So, I think it's important that they appreciate, you know, what players have done and that they understand, you know, some of the greatness about these players that have played. >> Reports, you kind of give them like a book report kind of deal. >> Oh, absolutely. Absolutely. We're going to give them how's it work? Just absolutely. They they they they get a a report assignment and they have to come up in front of the group and present that report to the group. >> And the group Well, it's to the group now. They'll either thumbs up or thumbs down the report. I don't have anything to say about it. You know, that's that's the fun of the offensive line room. >> And what are these reports about? Are they from past >> could be anything? It could be it could be anything. >> But it's historical NFL stuff. >> Uh a little bit of everything. >> A little bit of everything. You know, we got to keep in there. That's the spice of life, right? To keep it interesting, right? >> Okay. Who gets to pick the topic? >> Uh, that's uh could come from the coaches, it could come from the players, could come from the vets, >> you know. So, it's uh it's fun. It's a good environment, you know. It's been a great environment. >> One of your rookies is he's a pretty bright guy. Ethan Onyama, right? Has a, you know, degree in what is it? Bio something. I don't even know what it is, but bioengineering or something. Has he has he done any of these rookie reports yet? Is he is he the straight A student? We haven't gotten that deep in the weeds yet about that, but we're we're certainly going to get there. >> Speaking of bets, what is it like to have like a Jake Matthews in the room and just what he's been able to do for this franchise and this team and how he >> Yeah. So, real honor for me to coach, you know, a player like Jake. Uh his lineage, uh tremendous respect, you know, for what he's accomplished as a veteran player in our league. Uh and then having his presence in the room means a great deal for the line. you know, his leadership, you know, you can't you just can't underestimate what that means and and and how it carries over from from week to week, meeting the meeting, you know, just watching those guys, how they prepare. Uh it's it's very impressive, you know, they're they're they're a true pro. They're they're consumate pros and they know how to get ready for a meeting. They know how to get ready for a practice and they do a great job on the field. And and that's where it really comes to fruition is when you watch these guys work. You know, they've been well trained. They they come off the ball, they work hard, they finish, they play with great effort. So when you have those intangibles working for you and and they show up in tangible ways, it means a great great deal. >> James Brock on a lot of reps here with that first. What have you seen from him just as a UDFA and adjusting to everything? >> Yeah, I'm really proud of the job he did today. You know, uh we had some veteran centers out, so he had to step up and step in and take over the controls and he did a great job. He was like the air traffic controlman today. So, he landed all the planes safely, which was great. Did a great job. >> It's a group that's had a lot of continuity uh over the years just with several of these guys. How do you balance wanting to kind of keep the continuity where you can versus >> putting some competition in place for guys to potentially earn starting jobs? >> Well, I think that that takes place in training camp. I think when when once we get there, uh you'll see the competition, the competitive drills come alive a little bit more. So, the evaluations are are they're they're truer, they're pure. Um, but I think it's always good to have competition at any position, every position. And and the way that the league is right now, you're filtering in young players. Uh, you're turnurning the bottom of your roster. You're trying to develop players, especially in the line. So, the value of developing a young offensive lineman that could play for you, I mean, monetarily, uh, it it just helps everything. Helps the cap, allows you to go get a better player at the skill position. Uh, so the more we can develop in that area, you know, not expend on a higher pick, that's I mean that's what everybody's shooting for. >> Is there is there a common adjustment that rookies specifically have to make when they get to the NFL? Uh, especially maybe when you were to compare the rookies and the types of rookies that we saw in offensive line coming up 10, 15 years ago just with the way the college game has changed. >> Yeah, I think it's really different. I I I would say to you um because of the uptempo offenses in college football, they're not as developed. Now, that's not a knock on the coaches. It's just because of the nature uh of their environment. You know, they recruit a lot. You know, there's a lot of pressure to recruit. Uh the tempo offenses don't get the linemen, you know, doing a lot of individual drills. So, it's really like an assignmentbased offense. And a lot of times coaches are, you know, they have a good player, but they're always trying to get their the bottom of their line better or or the back end of their line better. So they don't spend as much time where here we can spend time with everybody and develop everyone, you know, because we have that luxury there. They don't they're kind of strapped with time. So it really hinders some of the development, but once they get to this level, you know, it's all day long. So it's it's it's profitable in that regard. >> You're from Japan, right? Like you were raised in Japan. Uh, >> born there, lived there till I was seven. Yes. >> What do you remember about it? >> We we lived off base. So, I basically spoke English at the house, but spoke Japanese while I was uh >> off base, you know, with all my friends. >> You remember any Japanese? >> Um, I do. So, like I said, my mom was Japanese. So, in the house, she would normally talk to me in Japanese and I would answer back in English, especially when we moved to America. And then uh in 96 I actually went back and I coached a at a Japanese team for two years. It was a Japanese corporate team. And so my Japanese uh it came back pretty quickly. >> What's the quality of play like over there? It was the recruit seagulls, wasn't it? >> Oh, yeah. I did my research. >> You did do your research. Uh so I always say it's kind of like division three kind ofish football. So our linemen, like our linemen were about 240 lb, 250 lbs. Those were our big linemen. Uh, but the skill the skill guys were pretty good. >> So, how did you end up back over there and what led you to come back to the States? >> So, I was coaching at Fort Lewis College. I was the offensive coordinator there and I was at the uh AFCA convention and one of the guys that was a head coach of one of the Japanese teams uh sat down and you know he just needed a seat so he sat with our staff and said, "Hey, do you know anybody that can coach quarterbacks?" and everybody pointed at me at the table and it says, "Oh, I coach a team in Japan." I said, "Oh." So then I started talking a little bit Japanese and go, "Oh, we should get together." And uh got together and and uh yeah, long story short, I ended up uh going there and coaching for him. >> Then your NFL start here. >> It was. It was. I did a couple internships uh with the 49ers and Chargers. And one of the internships with the 49ers, I worked with Jim Mora. He was the offensive defense coordinator. And then uh when he got this job, he said, "Hey, RP, you want to come out to Atlanta?" And so I came here and I was the offensive assistant in 2004. I was there 2004 56. All this has changed, I would imagine. >> You know what? Uh it's changed. There's been additions to it. >> Yeah. >> Okay. I got you. I saw when you were with the Lions, you were the chief energy officer at one point. Uh >> yeah, you know, I try to bring a little juice. Uh, I was kind of the the juice guy, you know, just have a little fun and try to put some energy into the practice. So, yeah, one of the guys said, "Hey, RP, you're the CEO, chief energy officer." >> Where's the energy come from? >> You know what? I I try to coach the way I'd want to be coached. Um, and the way I look at it is like, hey, you know, a guy that brings energy and, you know, lets me know what's happening. So, I always tell the guys, hey, you're going to know when I like it and you're going to know when I don't like it. And, uh, you know, that's what I try to do. just one about um the players you have here uh with Zakius. What do you guys like about him this spring? What have you seen from him out here so far? >> Uh Zakias uh one, he's a true pro and he and he helps the whole room uh get better. Obviously out here, you know, he's been playing in the slot, but he's smart enough to play anywhere. Um >> he is does a great job of uh I say not just running the line. So we might have a line that looks like you go five yards and out and he understands how to make that line come to life and and you know find a little space. >> Being in this role with the Dolphins last year does that kind of help like the familiarity now here as well? >> Uh you know with Tua uh yeah we were able to build a relationship while I was there and uh you know I love Tua. Um it's just a different offense so he's learning and I'm learning and uh yeah we're learning together. First impressions of Zachariah Bridge. >> You know, Zachariah uh >> the thing with him is uh he wants to be great and I and I truly mean that. He texts me all the time whether he wants to know something about what happened in practice this last practice or he's texting me about the next practice and hey RP, what do we got this next practice and what I got on this route and all this kind of stuff. But yeah, he wants to be great. >> What are the challenges of having left-handed quarterback and you'll have two here and you've obviously worked for two before. So what are those challenges for the receivers? You know, I I don't know how much how much of a challenge it is. I mean, I guess the ball spins a little bit different. Uh but it's funny because I'm a lefty. Drake's a lefty. We have a bunch of lefties. >> A lefty is a lefty. >> Yeah, we might have more left-handed people on this team. Uh rarely do you have two left-handed quarterbacks, but uh >> What What makes it different as far as like the spin? Like so like since I made the catch like cuz we were talking to Jan Dawson uh you know, a few minutes ago here and he said the first time that he he caught a ball from Tua, he was like, "Oh wow, that really is that's legit." like it really is different. >> Yeah. I mean, obviously it spins the other way and I probably, you know, leans a little left as it comes out, you know, >> but they're professional passers, so we we'll be professional catchers and it'll be all right. >> Shouldn't be a big deal. >> How'd you end it up in Atlanta? >> The first time around >> uh the spring. So, uh, >> um, I was, uh, still in a contract with, uh, the Dolphins and, uh, the Falcons put in a request and, uh, I think >> the Dolphins decided that they were going to let me speak to, uh, Atlanta and that's how it came about. >> Do you have any prior ties with the staff, >> Kevin, or anybody? >> No. No, it just um his receiver coach that was in >> in uh Cleveland uh he hit me up and he goes, "Hey, RP goes, I'm I'm going to go to Kansas City." And I told Kevin that he should try to get you if he can. And then so um I said, "Yeah, that's fine." You know, I'll talk to him. And so he put in a request and uh once that request got approved um then I was able to talk to him. >> How much Japanese do you speak? Uh, >> top a lot. >> A lot. Yeah. Like fluent. You're fluent. It's hard. >> Yeah. I can speak a little bit. >> Yeah. I I can speak. I can speak. >> Drop me off in Japan for a day and I'll I'll be all right. >> Wow. >> Okay. Best food. >> Favorite food in Japan? >> Great food. Great food. Japan. Uh, I'm a sushi guy. Okay. But I mean, I I'll eat all Japanese food.

title: Drake London, Kyle Pitts Sr. & other Falcons on growing team chemistry in OTAs | Press Conference
text: How's it feel to I guess kind of get back out there with some of the guys and just get rolling. New faces too. >> Yeah, it always feels good playing football. So, um yeah, just I don't like the weather right now. It's kind of muggy and hot, but >> it feels like training camp. >> Yeah, I know. Um No, but we're working right now and it's great to be back out here. >> What's uh Kevin Spansky like just as a a leader of men and and kind of what have you taken from from your time getting to know him a little bit over the last couple months? Yeah, I mean so far he's doing his thing and he just brings, you know, accountability and and honestly just pushing us to be the best that we can be right now. You know, we're never complacent. Um, and I think that's the big motto right now is just never be complacent at all and just keep on pushing forward and striving for greatness. And that's what he's kind of implementing it in like probably the most chillst way ever. But at the same time, he's like, we're about business and I love it. Uh, this wide receiver room looks very different than it did probably at the end of last season and in January. >> I was talking to, who was I talking to? It may have been Tanner or Tommy and they were talking about how many different elements they feel like they have within the room and um, I think that's pretty evident out here too. Um, your overall thoughts on what has kind of been built around you in the room and the excitement level that you have to to work with these guys. >> Yeah, just ball players. I mean, Jan, you got Oz back, which I'm stoked about. Um, CB, you got ZB. Um, I mean, you could go down the list really. Drum, Casey. I I think we just have a lot of versatile guys that are kind of right now, like I wouldn't say Jan or Oz or anybody like that, but guys who also too like are flying under the radar a little bit, who can really really bowl. So, I'm really excited for them to go out there and showcase that and and just show the team their value right now. Yeah. >> Is there any difference in catching a ball too as opposed to Michael? No, they're both lefties, so it's pretty much the same. >> Same spin. >> Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. >> I was going to ask about Tua. I don't know if we've talked to you since he's obviously been a part of the team. What's it been like working with him? >> Good. Um, he's a great dude. Always got a smile on his face. Very, very chill. Throw up the shot a little bit and we get rolling. So, now he's a great dude and and him and MP are getting along very, very well. And both of them are just competing and working really hard together and I love it. What is the key to, I guess, building that connection with another quarterback, I guess, trying to find that balance, of course, as they're continuing to have a quarterback battle themselves. >> Yeah, just catch the ball whenever they throw it. That's the biggest thing I try to pride myself on. Um, not really taking too long to mess or gel with a quarterback. Um, I take pride in that. So, yeah, whenever they throw the ball, I just try to make them right. Um, yeah, that's pretty much it. >> I know a lot of it is connection based, also recognizing where you like to be and where you like to throw it to. Do you have a lot of those conversations now or do you wait until it's just kind of who is the guy or it's not really matter? >> No, you got to have those conversations right then and there because you don't know it's football. It's not a matter of of of if it's a matter of when when you get hurt, you know? So, like you got to be ready and be on P's and Q's with everybody else as well. >> Uh RP, what's it like working with somebody who he's he's coached some of the the best. I mean, I imagine that he's really great to work with. >> I love RP. Yeah, RP is freaking hilarious. He just brings the juice out. Um, the way I can explain it the the best, I mean, I didn't know how old he was, but >> he's old. No, he don't look old. He don't run old. He don't do none of that stuff. Um, but he's just happy to play ball every day and come out here. So, it just kind of puts me in the mindset of like, why why shouldn't I be happy? You know, I'm youthful. I can run around, actually, get to go play and put the helmet on. So, what's the point of me being mad or or coming out here sluggish, you and that's what he brings to the table and into his smarts and stuff like that. But no, RP's that dude. >> Yeah, I I love talking to him. He's so smart. Like I love it. >> Be doing our jobs. We need to ask you about your acting, >> huh? >> After the release video, >> how fun was that? >> It was cool. Um I'm like a three take wonder. So I did pretty decent. Um took a little bit of Hollywood out of me, but that's probably the last time you'll see that. since we saw it. But uh practice today, what's the hell like >> dude, for our president to be down here and throwing the ball and and doing all that stuff, I think that's the dopest thing in the world. I think it's really really cool. And then too, just to hear from him, I mean, he's played with literally the greats who have come through here, Rody and and Julio. So to hear him um speak about, you know, their routes or what he saw with them and stuff, just soaking everything in is is really really cool to see. Yeah. Yeah. >> Could he could he still play a little bit? If if pressed, could Matt Ryan still get in there and play a little bit? >> Oh, I know he's itching all the time. Anytime he gets his hand on the ball, he wants to throw it. He wants to do something. I know he's itching and it never leaves your body. So, um Yeah. Yeah. >> I know I know you spoke a lot to Mike last year. How much time have you had that two sit down and just talk and just pick his brain about his philosophies and that? >> I mean, not too much. I mean, I know he has a family and stuff, so once he's out of here, he he he goes home to his family and things like that and spends times with them, but when we're out here on the field or or we're in the facility and stuff, we definitely sit down and talk about, you know, what's going on, what we see and everything like that. So, um, it's building. The chemistry is building with both of them. >> So, uh, you're throwing it back to 2021 with Matt Ryan throwing passes to you, man. >> Yeah, it's a nostalgic moment. It's great having Matt out here and, you know, he can still spin it like he can still play. So, it's it's pretty cool to see. >> You you had the chance to to play with him and now he's president of football. What are some of the things that are still the same about Matt Ryan and what are some things that are different? >> He still talks the same. Um he's very rash. Uh that won't ever change. That's Matt. But, uh different. He's just in a different role. He's still the same person. He's still, you know, I feel like is wrapping me tighter under his wing from a different perspective as a front office guy now. But he just has a different role. I mean, he's still leading the team in some sort of way, but just not physically. >> Yeah. Still competitive >> 100%. >> How do you think that would benefit the team knowing that you play with him, you know, how he was as leader as a quarterback, but now the fact that he's leading the team from another a different role? >> Yeah. Well, personally, I feel a little more happier because I know him more personally rather than some of these younger guys and rookies who just know him as Matt Ryan. I got a chance to play with him. But, uh, it's it's cool to see and and, you know, have him around the building and him just be able to pour into everybody that walks around. >> Did you stay in touch with him after he left here? >> Yeah, definitely. Yeah. Pretty awesome. >> Yeah. So, you know, love seeing the little cubes come up and they got Cal now. I don't know if he's I think he's the third cube. So, that's pretty cool. >> What have you seen from Michael Penn Jr. and just what how early he's been able to come out here and compete after having surgery? >> It's it's it's neat to see. Mike's one of my closest friends and just to see him go through his rehab and how he attacked it and now everybody thought he wasn't going to be ready and look at what he's doing. So, it was great to see. I love to be beside him competing and you know I'm I'm eager to see how this thing goes. >> What's this offseason been like for you? What you kind of working on as you get ready for another year? >> Everything. There's no one specific thing. It's always uh physical obviously in offseason until you get in here and you you know try and be mentally sharper, but uh just being able to trying to get strong faster. It's the same same goal every year. What what's the difference between catching ball from the two quarterbacks? >> They're both leftanded. >> There's no difference. >> Same spin, same everything. >> They're both left-handed. Yep. >> We just heard from Tua and his receptions of of the Falcons. What have been your first >> of him? >> Tua is a little more funnier than I thought. >> You know, I got to give it to him. Um he he he like to crack jokes a lot, but when it's time to work, he works. He's very smart. Um, hearing it from his perspective is is pretty cool. So, um, just, you know, eager to play beside him and, you know, whoever gets the job. >> What kind of jokes? >> I don't know if I can let those out. >> Says he's a good fit. What makes him do you feel like he's a good fit for him? >> That's what coach the fans said. I'm just going to roll with it. I'm I'm a competitor alongside whoever they put out there. Um, and I just want to win. coach said earlier today that uh he's happy with how you've embraced some of the newer things they expect of you to do. Could you shed some light on some of these new new things that you're doing now? >> Uh yeah, just I would say there just I would say adding more tools to my toolbox let me do a couple more things in terms of uh maybe route running and just schematically um being able to try and be a you know an asset in this offense. I actually don't think that we've talked to you since the franchise tag and and what did that mean to you to to get the franchise tag especially with all the turnover all the new that that was happening. What was that moment like for you? >> I mean I took the positive in it and uh Ian taking a chance and basically kind of like a my fifth year option but it's a six year option. Um and it's a blessing to be able to get that year and them not you know say h well you can go test it the market or whatever. trusty that you know we see something in you and it's it's pretty cool to see it's a new year and I'm just I'm not worried about it. It's already signed and it be cool. It's going to be a great year. >> Have there been any discussions about a contract extension of any kind at this point? >> That's that's a a my agent question. >> Would you want that to happen? >> I just want to win. That's all. >> To to Mark's question about this offense. I mean it's kind of been talked about Kevin Stfansy's offense is kind of very tight end friendly. Have you uh seen that so far and what's been presented to you? I would say we're just we're we're all learning the offense as a whole. Um it's it's not being anything more heavily, you know, one-sided than the other. Uh I do see there is a different, you know, a bunch of flexibility throughout the whole offense. So, it's cool to see. And, you know, tight ends, he he does like him a little bit. >> Uh Kevin Koger is, you know, continuing on as as your coach, your position coach. How much does that kind of mean to you to kind of have that continuity? I know we've talked to Bjon about how important that was for him and Michael Petri. How about you and Kevin? >> I think it's great um in having a guy who I knew and I feel like the year I had last year and how we've had some or the past two years how we've had our ups and downs and how he's been able to keep me even kill through, you know, sun and the the rain. So that's my guy. I appreciate, you know, all the work that we've been putting in and, you know, him helping me be a better player and on and off the field. So he his one quote is don't be a allstar human on and off the field. So that's that's something that you know that sticks with me and just trying to do that every day. >> Have you noticed any differences just between OTAAS and like you know different coaching staffs and things like that? Have you noticed anything different maybe about how this one is run compared to other OTAAS or anything like that? >> I mean yeah they're all different. All coaches are different. Um definitely everyone's detail oriented is just you know trying to play smart and you know just take our game to a new level and and come together as one. >> Having two co former coaches now coming with a new coach in this OTAA has it changed your approach and are you more um prepared for this now for the change? >> I wouldn't say my approach changed at all from coach to coach is more so come in there ready for myself and you know whatever they have to throw at you just roll with the punches. What have you learned from Austin Hooper in the short time you've got kind of gotten to know each other? >> Actually, a lot. Uh Hoop is very, you know, he went to Stanford, so he's he's very he's gifted and hoop he's he's he's on going on year 11. So, that tells you a lot that he's be able to sustain and play at a high level for 11 going on 11 years now and he's he's very mentally sharp. So, it's it's cool to hear some things on how I can think quicker on the field and see things quicker and uh that'll allow me to play faster. Do >> you have any like little nuggets aside from that? Like anything? I would say some some nuggets that won't that won't be put out in the media. >> How are you just feeling physically? Like do you feel like you're at your best shape coming in or how would you describe yourself? >> I feel great every year. Um definitely maturing more coming into my I guess you'll say m maturer body. Um getting a little older and you know finding different ways to continue to keep my body at a premium and my nutrition and recovery and all of that plays a part. >> You you obviously had a great season last year.
