And and I think the guys have have uh done just that. They're they're working like crazy. They're pushing each other. Um, and we're going to make sure that we're everything that we do, whether in the weight room, on the field, in the meeting rooms, is intentional about getting better at something. Even even the small things, the fundamentals and techniques, as boring as that can be to talk about, uh, we're going to make sure that we never lose sight of that in in this offseason program. >> When it comes, you were talking about Michael Pennock Jr. and stacking days. So, has he been able to go every day or is he getting like an extra day of rest or >> He's gone every single day. Yeah, he's done a nice job. And then how do you evaluate him at this point when he is coming back from an injury? Like what are you looking at from him on the field? >> Yeah, I you have to be careful not to forget that when evaluating any player where they are in the stage of a rehab rehab for instance and Mike in this case uh you you are understand that he's not 100% not to say what you know hard to put a number on it but knowing that his rehab is what takes precedent uh everything he does uh you take that with in mind. Um, having said that, just very impressed with everything he's doing uh on the field and in the meeting room as well. >> What have you seen from Tua just early early on in this process? >> Uh, working very hard, veteran, uh, fits in really well with our guys. Um, skill set is is what you see from his Miami days to now. Uh, very accurate, uh, but fits in really well. >> You're given to us a concussion history. Any limits on him as far as practicing or anything like that? >> No limits, >> non-cont and everything we're doing. >> You mentioned too is very accurate. He has that history on the field. Can you diagnose that? What what what makes a guy um what's the separator there? >> Well, I think it's it's the most important trait at the position as we've always talked about. Uh some guys get better uh at it with tweaks to their how they throw the ball, tweaks to how they uh their lower body, those type of things. But there is an innate ability of all and all of our guys have this, all of our quarterbacks have this to be able to let the ball go and and it's going where you want it to go. And um not to say that you're not going to miss throws in this profession. you're going to miss throws. But all of our guys possess that innate quality of of letting it go and and and knowing where where they want it to go. Uh but yeah, I think Tua just in his career, as you've seen, uh just has that innate God-given ability, >> even though he's on a he's on a new team and he's a veteran, but what have you seen from his leadership that stood out so far? >> I think all of our guys are uh being true and authentic to who they are. Uh you Tua no different. You're you're new to the building. you're new to the football team. I I think a lot of times you're getting to know your teammates is is where we are in this portion of of team building, if you will. So, uh, opportunities for the for our players to get to know each other, uh, happen on the field, happen outside of this building. Uh, so I I've just been impressed with, uh, Tua everything he's doing in in the meeting room on the practice field in being, you know, true to who he is. Uh but you know it's it's something where those type of things are organic and they happen over time. >> Do you expect Avon Terrell to be active in team stuff today? >> He will do some work. Yes. >> What's been your early assessment of Kyle Pittz? >> Uh Kyle's uh again a guy that is is here working like crazy. Uh takes coaching. Obviously the the physical skill set is obvious when Kyle's on the field and uh with how big he is and how he moves. But I've been impressed with what we're asking him to do and and couple new things for him. Uh, you know, as as your players continue on in their career, you want to find out more, you know, what else is in there and what else can we do and what can we help you with? So, I think Kyle's been uh outstanding in that regard of of trying to continue to get better in in so many areas. >> Anything uh you can share with us as far as new things that he's working on? >> All the above. Yeah. To be a he's trying to be the best version of himself. be the the most complete player at his position. Obviously, he's had some great great great moments in his young career and we're trying to build off of those. And also, like any player, there's always things you can work on. So, it's it runs the gamut really what what we're working on. What's >> it been like for you getting to know Jake Matthews and just how valuable is it to have a guy like him on the offensive line with his experience? >> Extremely invaluable. Uh he he's a pros pro. Fun to watch him out there. Uh Jake doesn't say much, but I think there's such great leadership in in guys that just do it the right way. I've been around some great leaders that you don't have to be rah. You don't have to be leading the team huddle before the game, but uh doing something and and doing it at a high level and and continuing to be a professional in everything you do. That's what I see from Jake on a day-to-day basis. >> Mike is the guy I believe you were with in Minnesota, right? I'm curious what you recall about him then and kind of what you see from him now here. >> Yeah. Well, I was on the staff. Mike was on >> defense and and obviously was a young player. We drafted him uh there. But, you know, you don't play this long at that position without being a really good football player. And I think his game has continued to grow over the years. Uh but just so impressed with Mike, how he um obviously number one job as a corner is to cover and just how he covers, but also how he he tackles, how physical Mike is uh is really impressive to me. >> Obviously being around the league, you you had some impression of who Be John Robinson was as a guy. I'm wondering if at any point did you think, you know, I wonder if all of that could be real, can be who he is, and after spending a month with him, what your impression of it is now. Well, I I was cautioned by people that you're not going to think this guy's real when you talk to him. And I think you guys have all experienced that. And that's who he is. It's it's that's just that's who Bjon is every single day. Uh how he approaches life, how he approaches people. Uh he's just he's got that authentic way about him. uh been fun to watch him work out here and and the physical skill sets, you know, what he's capable of doing and and you see it on tape, you see it on the grass even now, uh is really really impressive. And then it's the person off the field, uh you know, the the impact that he has on our locker room, which is really impressive. >> Kevin, I know you mentioned um footwork last week is an area to quarterbacks, but I believe Tommy mentioned kind of like the eye placement as well. when you're learning a new offense in your experience like how big of a factor is that eye discipline component and knowing or teaching the quarterbacks this is exactly where you look and when >> extremely important and when you sit in defensive meetings you hear defensive coaches talk about quarterback's eyes and where they're looking and young quarterbacks oftentimes will uh you know telegraph where they're going on a given play based on where their helmet is looking based on where their eyes are. So what you're trying to do at the quarterback position often times is manipulate the defense and uh not always you know cuz if you always look away then that's a tell. So uh there are certain concepts where we want to go aggressive with our eyes away from the intent. There are other times where we have to get our uh you know our eyes to the to the progression because there's a time where we may have to work all the way across the board left or right on a sprinkler head read as coach Van Pelt calls it you know. Uh, so I think there's so much that goes into the nuance of that position and certainly where you put your eyes are so important and I've been blessed to have been around some great quarterbacks but some great defensive players too where in seven on sevens they're they sometimes go opposite where the quarterback's looking and it's just it's that next level u of play from linebackers from safeties where where they they're playing the game within the game as >> How valuable is it to have Billan on your side? >> Uh extremely uh valuable. uh coach is somebody that you know having worked with before I know the impact that coach Callahan can have on your offensive line room on your offense on your offensive staff. Uh so somebody that I lean on quite a bit former head coach and coach Callahan so he's he's definitely uh a resource for me and as a young coach as I've been uh doing this and and and somebody that I can lean on. But uh he's a great great great technician. I think he's outstanding at developing players and uh as you watch coach work and watch our players work, uh it's it's you know there's no secret to improving. You have to just be out there and and uh do what your coach is asking you to do and also just uh try to hone in those techniques and coach is obsessed with the techniques of it. So it's it's fun to watch those offensive linemen work. Coach Devine Diablo landed on this team last year and was a vital part of the defense and when he was out the defense you could tell. Tell us about what you want to make sure you get from this season. >> Yeah, very impressed with Dine. Uh somebody that we've gotten to know here over the last few months, wired the right way, very very intelligent. I don't think you can overstate how important it is to have that intelligence right in the middle of your defense, right in the nerve center, uh if you will. Uh so to have somebody like Deine who's uh c can can can can run sideline to sideline, can tackle, can play in the pass game, but can also uh align your defense, it's a calming influence on your defense and your head coach. When you have a guy who's in the middle of the defense and and everybody understands what their roles and their responsibilities are because he's clear in in how to deploy the defense. >> But the guys next to Divine Diablo, have you seen anybody start? It's really early in the process, but what have you seen those guys? um Christian Harris in guys like that >> like you said very early we're rotating so many different guys in there uh throughout the walkthroughs throughout the individual periods throughout 707 team if you will so I think that's the name of the game at linebacker and and also where we are as a as a team just rotate guys in and out uh see what type of combinations make sense and and give guys as many opportunities as they can uh to to put their best foot forward let us have a real evaluation of them over the course of this offseason program leading into preseason football as well. >> And on that note, is there an expectation to see Troy Anderson potentially in this process just during OTAAS or or >> uh I'd say we'll work through it. Uh not practicing this week, but we'll work through that. >> Any update on Billy Bowman? I know he >> uh similar uh doing very well. You know, all these guys are are in different spaces of of their rehabs, but really really impressed with how they've all worked and Billy is right there uh making sure that even though he's maybe not getting a full speed rep, he's right in the in the thick of it, making sure he's not missing out on any mental reps, but doing a terrific job in his rehab. >> Up to this point, what have you learned about your rookie class and how are they adjusting? >> Uh what have we learned? We've learned uh they've they've done a nice job in everything we've asked them to do. And and when I say that, I mean some of the simple things, being where you're supposed to be when you're supposed to be there. Uh these guys are very very conscientious. Uh don't have to light a blowtorrch under any of them, if you will. They're they're working uh they they fit in culture-wise in that regard. And I think it's, you know, important that the young guys look into in their position rooms, look at the guy that that's been in that room for eight years, 10 years, and how does he approach his job? And I think by and large our our rookies have done that and have identified the guys on on the roster that they can uh see how a pro does it. So I've been very impressed in that regard on the field and and those type of things. That's it's so early to to say those type of things, but just how they've approached their job now that it's their jo uh I've been impressed. >> Um kind of old news, but when schedule came out a couple weeks ago, I don't even remember if we asked you about it. Uh what are the first things that you look for as the head coach? I don't like, you know, for a lot of us, we're very, you know, excited to kind of see what it looks like. >> You're looking at restaurants you want to go to different cities. Uh we always look at I think the schedule comes out, you look at where your by-week is, you know, where those prime time games are, uh where the division games are. I I think I always say this, how you feel about the schedule in April, May, now how you feel about it in May is totally different than how you feel about it come February of next year. So, uh, really you're looking at the travel schedule for your football team. Uh, do you have backto-backs, road games, those type of things, but, uh, you know, so much can change between now and those games. So, you don't want to overthink that either. >> I want to ask about that specifically because I know you're a logistical guy with the three consecutive prime time games. Is that something is that a challenge that you have to work through? Um, >> I I would not No, I don't think it's a challenge. I think it's it's a great opportunity. I think our guys, ask anybody, they love to play under the lights and and they love that uh exposure, if you will. Uh but uh no, not a challenge. Uh it's a challenge for our logistics team here and who would do a great job for us. But uh uh we we we love any opportunity we have to play uh really at any time slot, but uh just like our guys grew up playing on Friday nights that they love playing under the lights as well. >> Any Cleveland records? >> I have some good ones for you. Yeah, you have to wait though. What have you seen from Jaylen Walker just um as he's going into year two looking to develop and continue to build? We we we talked to him last week. Just the energy, you can feel it. What have you seen from him? >> You know, Jaylen's a guy that we got to know when I was in Cleveland in that draft process, that pre-draft process, and and every team that spent time with him really um came away with thinking that this is a player that loves football, loves it, and loves his teammates. And that's what I've seen from him. Now, there's things that we're working on and and he and coach Timu have done a great job of of working in these individual periods and different things to do whether it's in the run game or the pass game. But, uh it's fun being around a young man who's wired like that, uh who's wired to put the team first, uh to push his teammates. And it's no surprise just his upbringing and how he was raised in this uh in this profession in some ways in with his dad and uh just being around football as much as he's been around. He's just uh it's it's uh great to watch that young man work. >> What do what do you think that what what would you like his emphasis to be just kind of as he continues to develop? >> Uh very um in development. I think we're we're we're a daily development type of program. So there's things that he's walking out in the field right now thinking that he wants to get better. And it's it could be, you know, his his get off on on on run plays. It could be how he stabs uh you know and and disengages blocks. It's it's so it can be so technical. So that's where I would say for our our guys as coaches, we we have uh improvement plans, if you will, for every single player. And that can be whether you're a 12-ear vet, a rookie, a second year vet in the case of Jaylen. And uh we have we want to identify all these little things uh that that we can help you get better at because we know all those little things add up to the big thing. >> He's in that spot right now, too, that leap we hear all about. What do you think kind of drives that year one, year two lead >> from his from all positions? >> All positions. Yes. >> I think there's something to be said for sophomores in in this game of football and in in the pros where you've you've had that lap uh if you will and and and you now know you have your bearings and you know what this game's a little bit about. The speed of the game and those type of things. And then just a comfort level in schematically I think can doesn't happen overnight sometimes. So, I I do think there's a general uh leap, if you will, from that first year to that second year, just based on your comfort in in everything that you're doing. >> One more. >> Okay. Thank you guys. Appreciate it.

title: Jack Campbell Contract Extension Press Conference | May 27, 2026
text: Well, uh, I guess I just like to start off, um, and just say thank you to the Lord for giving me the my, uh, unique talents and abilities and putting me here. I think he has me in Detroit for a reason. Uh, ever since I got drafted here, I'd like to thank my family. Um, my wife, my four parents, uh, Kyle, Drew, Sydney, Brady, and Katie, uh, grandparents, just all the influential people throughout my life, uh, that have got me up to this point. Um, and it's it's it's a point I guess where honestly like people think that it's going to change like like you wake up and you have like everything you ever dreamt of. But you I can tell you this much like I woke up and I still have the same problems. I'm still Jack Campbell. So for me it's just added fuel to my fire. Um, I'm super grateful for the to the organization, the Lions, Brad, um, Rod Wood, Diz, Charlie Atkins, all the people behind the scenes who helped me through this whole process. And then, of course, the Ford family, uh, Miss Sheila. Uh, I'm just super grateful that they uh, saw something in me and believed in me and wanted to keep me around. So, I mean, I'm just super grateful to all them. Just the whole process was super professional. um they treated me like I would like expect like I feel like you guys would expect them to treat a a great player in this um organization and you can see all the people before me and how they've treated them. So um just super grateful for the opportunity to come out here and have um a couple more years with the guys here. I'd like to thank uh Dan uh Shep and Ham. I feel like those are probably the three guys that I probably relate to the closest on a daily basis. um they've pushed me and molded me into a player um that I feel like I uh sometimes didn't see and they showed me that I was that player. Um yeah, so I mean it's just really surreal and I can't thank enough people. Uh my agent, he did a fantastic job. Chase, uh I'm super grateful for you and to the fans. Uh, I'm just super grateful and excited to have the opportunity to put it on uh and go out there and um truly give you what you want to see. And I feel like that's a thing uh that's kind of opened my eyes is just people how much they care about the team and how the team is just the heartbeat of the city. Uh we're in a city full of working-class people that just every single day grind it out. Um, so I feel I feel for those people because I I I see firsthand like my brother back home. I see how hard he works. I see how growing up I saw how hard my parents work for what they got. So, um, I just got a deep appreciation for people who show up to work every single day, even if no one notices, even if no one writes stories about them. Uh, get to work, do their job, and take care of their families and keep their family first. Uh, just a great appreciation. And I mean, that's literally what the the city of Detroit epitomizes. Um, so that's what I'm going to try to epitomize. Just that that's how I was raised. That's how I guess I see life and that's my perspective on things. Um, so I mean, you guys already know what you're going to get from me. Um, every single day, nothing less than um the standard, which is I'm setting we're setting the standard at the highest level this season. Um, and yeah, that's pretty much it. I'm just super grateful and um get to be around a little bit longer. So, I'll take that. Yeah. >> Yeah. >> Jack, you talked about, you know, just this contra adding fuel to your fire to continue to work hard. >> You always been like seem like a self motivated person, >> but you come to Detroit and you hear the outside noise with you being selected so high >> and then you able to, you know, have come to this building where they believe in you to actually pick you that high. How was it to just go through that, experience that, I mean, and fight through that, and then get to this point now where you kind of you kind of proved everybody wrong. >> Uh, yeah, it's funny. I remember that. Uh, like it was yesterday. Uh, it was just a big moment in my life. I worked and achieved what I wanted to achieve, which is to make it to the NFL. Um, I kind of had a nearsided vision. Like, I didn't think it would turn into this at first. Uh, and I feel like that's kind of at least my perspective on things, kind of what you got to do. like I got to go earn a spot now. I can't come into this thinking like I'm going to be an allp pro, right? First, like it just steps to everything. Um, so when I got drafted on draft night, yeah, I remember everything. I remember a lot of things that were said. Uh, a guy from my hometown mailed me a letter. I still have it today. Just the, uh, CBS sports article just talking about how like this is probably the worst pick in the NFL history. And I'm just like, you guys are for sure. Um, so I mean all that stuff like it wasn't about proving them wrong. I feel like for me it was proving the people who believed in me right and that ever like started back at Iowa coming out of high school I only had Iowa State who like even wanted to recruit me like at the at the end Minnesota offered me. So like it's just something that I feel like I've carried along my whole life and um so it was really nothing new. I knew the type of player I was going to be. Um, I feel like in those moments that things weren't going my way, you just got to continue to remind yourself who you are. Um, and I feel like again like that kind of goes back like my family was huge in that whole thing. Um, a lot of people were praying for me. Um, my wife, she was right there beside me. So, like it's not just me who's doing this, it's everyone behind the scenes. And I I really do want to let like and that's what on a daily basis try to let them know like how appreciative I am because they saw just the progression all the way up until now. Um so I mean it's funny how things work. I don't get into all the stuff outside. People can think what they want to think at the end of the day. I know who I am as a person. I know who I am as a player. I know that the organization believed in me wholeheartedly. They saw something in me. And now it's up to me to choose what I'm going to do. And I feel like um in today's world, I feel like we need to maybe improve on that a little bit. >> That just a little bit the uh that story. I mean, was that a friend who sent that to you? Just a random fan. Do you have that like taped on the >> guy uh out of a different town? I played basketball against his son in high school and he sent me um just like a book, like a a dream big book. I was like, "Yeah." So, I get that in the mail. I don't know who this guy is. I'm like, "All right, sure." I open the first page. I open the first page and there's that letter in there and it like it's talking about like the uh draft analysis on things. And I look up and it's Jir Gibbs, F or Dao. So, I'm like, "All right, I feel pretty good about myself. I can't be like that." Like, I look down, it says F. is like, "Jack Campbell is probably the worst football player of all time." And I said, "Yeah, probably. You're probably right." But I saw uh I guess Brad Holmes saw something in me. And uh I guess the people who get to work with me see something in me. And I just try to be who I am every single day. And you just can't ride those those rides. You can't get too high. You can't get too low. Cuz now it's like I got people texting me like, "Bro, I always believed in you ever since." I'm like for no doubt you did for sure. But um I don't know. It's been it's been good. It's been just so good and it's been refreshing to just like have the again the support system around me. I don't have to worry about the outside noise. I know who I am. My family knows who I am at the end of the day. If I didn't play football, I'd be the same person. Um but I'm just super grateful to be in Detroit. And I like the fans are just um something that I hold near and dear cuz I just feel like this city is just so special and it's uh just reminds me a lot about like growing up and like the people who influenced me >> that do you ever like look at it like amra you know memorize the receivers that were you don't ever you just know that >> I just like looked at the thing I was more interested in the note and what I had to say but yeah there yeah there was a lot of things said but I mean I just >> Yeah. Yeah. and it always will be. Um, and that's something I have >> you ever shown Jir that story. He knows that he was also great in >> I don't know I don't know Jir's probably seen everything. Every time I see him he's on his phone >> and then he goes out there and does what he does. So more power to him. He's probably I mean he's probably seen this story but uh at least he wasn't the worst pig in the draft. So he might have been the second maybe. you've seen this team resign, you know, core players. >> When that happened, did you, you know, >> manifest like I want to be next and and to be part of that >> um blueprint that they have, draft, develop, resign? >> Uh, no. Coming in here, I was totally focused on myself to be quite frank with you. I feel like it obviously in the NFL if you don't perform uh you're kind of out. It's a business and I understand that and like I totally understand them uh declining my fifth year option because I know it's a it's a business thing and I have the utmost respect for how they feel. Me and Brad were I feel like communicating through the whole process. He was very professional about everything. I tried to stay professional with my situation and everything going forward. Um, so I feel like no, it was never about trying to be the next Paneet. Never about being the uh trying to be the next uh St. Brown, Hutch. I mean, you J Mo, Kirby, like all those. It was never about that. I feel like for me it was just being about the best player that I can be. And that was the whole focus this whole time. And it's going to be the continued focus. I guess now I just get the byproduct of like the fruits of my labor. Um, but yeah, no, it's it's never been about trying to be the next one. For me, it's been trying to prove the front office, right, and the pe people who have believed in me through my whole career, right, up until this point. >> Now that you're part of that group, is that I mean, does that feel good? Not that you rest on that, but obviously you're clearly part of the core. >> Yeah. No, I feel like I'm very appreciative that they believe in me and want me to be a part of the core. Um, so I mean for them to have that belief in me, I mean it only it only makes me more motivated um because I know that I'll be a part of something special um in the future and I have been. I don't really look uh in the past quite a bit like this whole career like I haven't really looked back but there's been some special teams that have come through here and we need to continue to keep that up. So um but it was never about being the next guy. I feel like for me it was always focus on like how can I be the best at what I do um and what I'm asked to do in Shep's scheme and in AG scheme and then how can I bring the guys around me to be the their their best best self. So >> we talked to him this offseason and he said this is Jack Campbell's defense no question about it's his defense that runs through. I'm just curious your thoughts when when a coordinator has that much confidence in you >> and and just how that relationship has has grown even more now than this off season. No, I've just been super appreciative of them. Um, I feel like now stepping into this off season. Uh, the last couple years I've been the youngest guy in the room, so it's been kind of a just a dynamic of like trying to earn the leadership spot, but like I'm still the young guy in the room, whereas now I feel like um get thrown into the fire, which is like what I want. Like I'll never forget like the best thing that ever happened to me in my career was my second year, everybody getting hurt. With all due respect to the guys that got hurt because I had opportunity to go out there, get bunch of game reps. They didn't care if I was doing good or bad. I was the only one left. So, go get your reps. So, like learning through that whole season and like what worked, what didn't work, how can I improve that. Um, I feel like that's where I guess probably I might have earned some respect in that aspect and taking on the load of uh being the main communicator out there. Um, now that I mean it's it's um it's nice to have it like be my defense, but again my perspective I don't think that your defense can be elite if you put it all on one guy. I want all the 11 guys to think that like they have a part of it and like they I want like in my opinion and this is just how I think if you don't think that it's your defense each 11 out there and like you take responsibility and like you have pride in what you're doing I feel like you won't be elite. Um, so it's just something that I've always kept to my I guess in my own head is like I've always thought that it's my defense, but now that it's this time of like it's really just me being out there like being able to lead and uh being able to find better ways to connect with guys so then I can uh help them out. Um I feel like that's where I got to take that next step this off seasonason um is to just make connections with guys to help bring them along. Um, and for me, I have no excuses. I've been in the system for 4 years now. Um, so messing up is not really okay at this point, and that's something that I try not to do. So, >> obviously, did you guys, now that you're back together, how did you guys kind of process last year not making the playoffs and how is that kind of driving you guys this year? >> Uh, I don't think about the past a lot, but it it definitely is a chip on your shoulder. And I'll say this, every single guy they brought in was for a reason. And every single guy that they brought in, I've been super impressed with. And I feel like you got you got to have the right mindset. Um, we're in a league now, I don't know if I should say this, but we're in a league now where like they don't really let you play the way that it probably should be played or the way it should look be look like look like on the field. So, you got to get guys with a mindset of just like, I'll do whatever it takes to win. And especially now with younger guys coming in. I mean, they've come from and this is just how it is. But a lot like the NIL people telling them how good they are. Like it's you just kind of got to learn to be at the bottom of the barrel and grind it out again and just learn like this isn't seven on seven that we're playing even though they're trying to make it that way. And you got to have a guy with the right mindset that like I'm gonna go like I don't know. It's just like it's a mindset that I really can't explain, but it's like you gotta like kind of be dark. The energy has been great. >> Um, seeing the guys from last year, Trader over there, just kind of keep growing up and learning ball and just wanting to just get better every single day has been incredible. Yeah. >> Is it different having the head coach come from your side of the ball? >> Different perspective. Um, yeah, absolutely. But I think it's he's coach Halfley's done a great job with talking scheme with both sides of the ball. Hey, offense, this is how we want to get attacked and this is defense. Um, so to be strong somewhere, you got to give somewhere else. So just learning that and talking through that with stuff with him as a team and individually has been awesome to kind of see his perspective. >> Zach, I got a question about how you see yourself fitting into this rebuild and um we know what you've done on the field. I saw you out there talking to Huntley and Biggers during practice counseling them. On the other hand, next year you'll be 31. Uh you'll have a big big salary cap number. >> Have you thought do I fit in here long term? Do you allow yourself to think that? Tell me about that. >> I'll think about that. I I told Zeke and them from day one. You can ask him. I told him, "Look, y'all are here to take my job. And that's my job, not to let you." Um, and there's no no hard feelings, no anything that happens there. If my home's not here, it's not here. But I really still feel like it's here. I love it here. I think my home's here. My wife and I love it down here. And we want to make a name. And I want to retire a dolphin. So, I'll do whatever it takes to stay here. It's been exciting. The fan base here is incredible. Uh, there's so much more to Miami than what you think of when you think of South Beach. There's uh the whole Everglades, the countryside, all that kind of stuff's incredible. So, we love it here. Um, and uh, I think these coaches have done a great job of I told them this year like, "Look, it's open open market, man. Go play. Go make a play. There's no uh, no ties to anybody. Go out there and win a win a job." And I think when you breed that competition, you start with that from day one. Uh, you can really do something special. >> Obviously, it's just May. >> Yeah. >> But at the moment, the team is listed as an underdog at 16 of the 17 games on the schedule. What is that like? >> What do you mean? What is it like? >> What is that like to put those expectations >> doesn't mean anything. What have you seen from him this spring? There's a smile on your face. I'm sure there's some good things to say about him. >> Solid. I think uh one of the first things he got in trouble for was squatting too much. Um the big uh big focus is taking individual to team and uh how to best I guess pose the drills to translate into team reps. So we're focused on that a lot this offseason and keep growing. >> And do you have like maybe an example personal story of that truth at a time when Jefferson coach was honest? >> Yeah. Uh he had the record. Yeah. But uh when I had that season I was like okay the NFL could be a possibility and then from there it was okay let's keep working. I had one more season at at Ferris uh did it last season got the league got drafted and then obviously now you start back from square one. So, um that that Cincy game coming down here getting some confidence going out there playing uh and getting that start was uh for that game uh with what three weeks left of the season that year um really kind of helped me I feel like catapult my career into what it became. >> Zack, how did you mentally compartmentalize this off season? You see a lot of the best players you came in. I'm sure there's natural indication I think about what it means for us. How did you and your family handle maybe that uncertainty period? My wife had a baby a our second baby August April 10th. Uh we're a little busy. Um but no, honestly, it's how I've always worked at my career and how at my job is that's out of my control. My tape was already out there from last season. The offseason was on. Enjoy the offseason. What happens happens and have the confidence and the uh the trust in God that hey, whatever does happen, I'm going to make the most of it. That's what I did when I came down here. Uh when I got cut that second time out of Baltimore, I ended up down here. Heck yeah, it was scary. But man, it's try to figure out a way to be the best person you can be every single day out there in that field. And you know, hopefully the chips fall as they may. >> Greg had this quote a couple months ago where he said like everybody's trying to check their ego at the door coming in the offseason program. Is that something that that you've noticed or have you seen just the removal of any ego? >> When you have a change up like we had with top to bottom um I mean everybody right you kind of you're you're starting to square one. So yeah, you are checking your ego. Look look I don't care what you did last year. it's what you can do this year and that's the whole point of the NFL is what can you do for me today. Um that's the way I live every single day, every practice, every play is, hey, last snap doesn't matter. It's the next time that matters. So just to keep working on that and keep driving forward, >> Zack, when you uh have that captain patch on your jersey, what does that mean to you? >> Yeah, when I've had it in the past and we don't have that yet, but uh means a lot. It means like the team, the guys put pride in saying, "Hey, look, we want him out there representing us as a team on and off the field to be the leader we rely on and a guy that we we fall for every single day that we're going to follow and trust." He's always here. He's always in the building. He's always asking questions. I mean, he practices so hard. He's so intentional. He's he's a smart football player who loves the game and he's been a lot of fun to coach. Um, again, right now we're playing in shorts and t-shirts and there's no contact and there's no tackling and but when it comes to taking what he's learning in the classroom and applying it on the field and being in the right spot and communicating and grasping the scheme um, and showing good leadership back there and being a great teammate and giving great effort and having a great attitude, I mean, I can go on about him. I think he's doing a a really really good job. Um, but when when anyone asked me right now, right, anyone being truthful to you, being truthful to anyone in our building, being truthful to my wife, um, who really doesn't ask me a lot of these questions, but maybe she she could like, how how are the guys doing? I mean, yeah, I think they're doing a good job in the setting that we're putting them in, but eventually when the helmet and shoulder pads come on, we'll find out who can make those plays, which ultimately the game is about. But for passing the test of what he's been given right now, I mean, I think he's doing a great job. >> How big is that communication piece considering that, you know, you told us that you'd like to run your defensive safeties? >> Communication is everything. >> Communication on defense is everything. I mean, you want it to be loud. Like, if you hear a loud defense, you you'll get a confident defense. >> Um, and that's thing that we have to strive for. But communication is going to be the key. And whether it's the Mike backer, the linebackers, the DNS talking to the tackles, but for the safeties, yeah, that's that's that's a big deal because they get everything set back there. >> Has uh 10 sacks in his first two seasons. Do you view his skill set as aligning with this scheme relative to high sack production? Do you see that in his future? >> I hope so. That would be that'd be great. Um, I see Chop right now as a guy who's driven to learn and improve his fundamentals, his techniques. I think Austin's done a really good job with him. Um, but that's got to be in the run game and rushing. This is not you're just going to rush or I'm not going to do that. He's got to play the run well, which I've been really proud of him. The way he's playing an individual and even in the walkthroughs how the Liberty's been and using his hands and getting his eyes in the right place and taking a good first step. Um, but you earn the right to rush by playing the run well and that's one thing I continually talk to him about and I think we'll see him do really well. Um, but yeah, we're counting on him that sack production we need. I mean, that's that's a skill set that he has and needs to be developed still. Um, and yeah, that's our job to put him in those situations to have the production and figure that out. >> Would you rather have two third down sacks or six third down pressures? Like one or the other? >> Depends. What did the pressures cause and what did the sacks cause? Did a pressure cause an interception? Because then I'd rather have the pressure than the sack depending on when it happened, right? Um is did the pressure force the quarterback to throw the ball away and now they're punting? Same with the sack, right? Did the pressure lead to a big play and didn't mean anything? And so just depends on what happened on the play. Jeff, regarding your kicking competition, um, will every single kick be tracked and which I assume it is, and what matters in the final analysis? Is it every single kick or only kicks in certain situations? >> I think it's both, right? I think it's it's looking at the big picture over time, the consistency, um, and then in the situations where, you know, there is pressure, who's coming through and making those kicks. But everything has to be evaluated. It's really it's it's the only thing that we have to base it off of right now is practice and then obviously when we once we get into training camp and joint practices and preseason games, we'll have to make a decision. Jeff, >> I want to ask you about leadership on this team. Obviously, you're new. You're trying to figure out people. You're trying to figure out personalities and you're also trying to lay your own foundation. How like how do you kind of evaluate where you are from a leadership standpoint on this team with the the veteran players? Because I've always had this belief that the young players not only learn from the coaches, but they also learn from the older veterans in their units. And you have no veterans in some of these units. >> Yeah. Then it's going to come from the coaches where we don't have those veterans, but there are some veterans that I think we have some really good leaders. Um, you know, I don't want to go through names right now and leave anybody out, but we have some we have some key guys that have played that are leaders. Then we have some secondyear guys that you can see are more comfortable and they're starting to lead in their way, right? I think that's really important for everybody to understand that there's so many different ways to lead. It could, like I said, it could be pulling a guy aside. It could be how you talk to a guy in your room. It could be behind closed doors bringing a guy along with you. It could be on the weekend bringing a group of the young guys out and doing something or inviting them over to a house for dinner, which we've had a lot of guys do, right? Um, and then there are rooms like I can't look in the eye and tell you there's there's an older leader in every room that's been there before and done it because we're young and that's just the reality of of who we are. And I said to the coaches today, there are some instances where I need I need the staff to step up and lead and then I need the staff to develop leaders and I have to develop leaders because I've been in too many places where a coach comes in and says, "We don't have any leaders around here." I think that's a bunch of BS, right? You can develop leaders. You can teach leadership. I can teach leadership to the staff. The staff can teach leadership to the players. We have to do that. I think that's key for this team to grow. Um, but to say you need x amount of guys in each room. I mean, right now we have who we have. So, what can we do about it to make it better? Um, and that's why I said to you right now, my the biggest thing I'm doing is I'm really observing and watching everything. I'm watching every guy. I'm watching every clip of film. And then in the team room, I'm trying to show them what's good, what's not good enough, what can be better, and which won't be tolerated. Right? And then the beautiful part right now is the guys have they've bought in and they're following. And it's so much fun to coach these guys right now because they're giving everything that they have and everything that we asked to do. And it's fun to come to work every day. So, you know, we'll keep working through that. >> That's good. >> You want me to hand you your recording?

title: Takeaways from Early Stages of OTAs | Big Blue Kickoff | New York Giants
text: Welcome to Tuesday's edition of Big Blue Kickoff Live here on Giants.com, YouTube, the mobile app. He is Matt Scitec. I'm Lance Meadow with you for the next 60 minutes as we break down all that is happening with the New York Giants. It is presented by Cadillac, the official luxury vehicle of the New York Giants as we are broadcasting from the Giants podcast studio presented by Hacksac Meridian Health. Keep getting better. 2019-4513 is the telephone number. You can also reach out to us individually on social media using #giants chat. He's at Matt Scitec. I'm at Lance Meadow, one word, last name, Me. We'll get to your comments on social media as well as your calls a little bit later on in the program. This is our first show since the holiday weekend. Hopefully everybody had a restful weekend and we did not discuss some of the takeaways from the press conferences last Thursday. So, Matt and I are going to delve into that. Also, there was an OTAA practice on Thursday. Since there was no show on Friday, we'll use that to take advantage of this. And let's start. To me, Matt, the most interesting thing that came out of the media sessions was John Harbaugh providing a bit of an update on the injury front. Now, remember, there's no physicality. There's no contact at this stage, but it's also an opportunity to get an update on players that may have had some injuries from the tail end of last season and where they are right in terms of their level of participation. And the player that I want to start with because he's been a big part of the dialogue on our show over the last few months and that is of course Malik Neighbors. So this was what Harbaugh said on the neighbors front. he's in the quote middle end quote of his rehab from the torn ACL. And Harbaugh added it's quote not a simple knee end quote and that essentially means it was a significant injury. He had indicated the goal is to get him out there in training camp, but nothing is concrete, Matt, at this point, and there's no definitive timetable, which once again is not earthshattering news, but it again emphasizes, okay, there's a reason why they brought in some established veterans in free agency, so that if neighbors, let's start, and once again, I'm just speaking hypothetically because nothing is defend definitive. If he starts out on PUP, the physically unable to perform list and spends the bulk of training camp and let's say is not ready, that rolls over to the regular season, he could potentially miss the first four games and they're going to need the veterans as well as some of the rookies to come in and step up to complement the tight ends with respect to passing options for Jackson Dart. >> Yeah, I mean, look, I was there when when coach said this on Thursday, and you know, this became a big news item. You know, a lot of national media outlets picked up on this and wrote about, you know, oh, Giants, you know, are now concerned about Malik Neighbors. >> This was what we like to call in this building a non-update update. John John Harour did not say anything that we did not already know. Like obviously we knew Malik suffered a serious knee injury. It has been already said before during either coach or Joe's press conferences that it wasn't just, you know, your standard ACL tear. there was more to it. So, I I heard this and then I saw it blowing up and I just I'm like, I don't really understand why. I mean, we this is nothing new. We knew all this information. John Harrow has said before and Joe has said before they hope that Malik Neighbors is able to get back on the field during training camp at some point. Not doesn't necessarily mean day one. you know, at some point during that month of end of July, month of August, they hope to get him back on the field. Again, nothing new. There's been no guarantees that he would be ready for week one. You know, every time that Joe or John have given a update on Malik Neighbors and Cam Scataboo, every single time it's been Scataboo is further along in his recovery and has a better chance of getting out there earlier than Malik. So, I I saw this and it's been blowing up and I'm just it's a little confusing to me because and I understand because we don't you know we don't get Malik updates every day obviously that I guess is that's why this got blown up as much as it did but >> and the national media also is not around the Giants on a daily basis too. So I think that's in fairness. >> So I just I wanted to get that out of the way first to say that. Uh, but yeah, the, you know, the biggest thing that I have said that I've been looking for this spring was Jackson throwing to his new pass catchers. And with Malik not being out there along with some other guys that we'll get into, but Malik obviously being the biggest name pass catcher that's not on the field, it's given Jackson a opportunity to start developing chemistry with those other I don't even want to call them secondary pass catchers because a lot of them are going to be starting for the or some of them will be starting at least for the Giants. But, you know, the Isaiah Likelys, who obviously we know last week made that incredible, insane one-handed grab, sort of mimicking the uh the Air Jordan logo, which I thought you would appreciate. >> Yes. >> Um he's obviously we knew he was going to be a big part of the passing game. Isaiah likely that's been on display in the beginning parts of these OTAAS. Uh some of the other wide receivers that the Giants brought in, you know, Darnell Mooney, Calvin Austin. I feel like Calvin Austin, we don't, at least I don't keep track of the number of receptions from each player during team drills, but I feel like Calvin Austin probably has the most catches of anyone during the first three days of OTAA practices. He's been targeted a lot. He's been catching just about everything thrown his way. Malachi Fields has made a couple of very impressive catches. Obviously, the the one we talked about on the the first day of OTAAS jumped up with one hand. Incredible catch. Uh but yeah, the first couple of days and for the rest of spring and even into the start of training camp, Jackson's going to get an extended opportunity to start building the rapport with these other pass catchers. And if the Giants want to have success on the field in 2026, those other guys are going to have to step up and play big roles in the passing game because as we said, we don't know if Malik will be ready week one. Even if he is on the field playing week one, he's not going to be 100% Malik Neighbors. He's not going to be the Malik that we're used to seeing. It's going to take him a little bit of time to get back to his old self. So, these other guys are going to need to step up and play big roles. So, it's good that that chemistry building has started already in spring. >> Yeah, that's the benefit of neighbors being sideline. It gives now ample time to your point for Dart to work with receivers that he has no established chemistry with. And I think it furthermore emphasizes that Mooney and Austin weren't just brought in to give the Giants bodies. They were brought in because they're respected veterans. Mooney specifically has a history with Matt Naggi and had a career year in the Bears system, but they feel that these players can be productive in the event that Neighbors absence rolls into the regular season. The other absence that you were alluding to is Darius Sllayen. And I would say this is new news. Harbaugh said that he was dealing with a sports hernia that he apparently was playing through and battling last season. And so he had surgery to repair that, but he should be ready to go for the start of training camp. So when you think about it, Matt, Dart is down his top two guys in Neighbors and Sladen. So opportunities galore for Mooney Austin Fields and even some of these other receivers, Isaiah Hajins and Gunnar Ovesky, who Paul and I were talking about last week about where does he fit into this equation? how hard is his pathway to make the roster because of his special teams value and so forth. So, this is the time where once again, you're running through routes. I love how Harbaugh calls this the fast rehearsal period, which is a very fitting term. You're trying to play at a high speed to somewhat simulate the regular season, but you know, you can't contact defensive backs can't get in the way of receivers. They can't disrupt routes. So that's why Harbaugh mentioned the ball really should barely touch the ground right during these sessions because it is ideal the environment for an offense to execute. Now we know that once again that doesn't always happen because sometimes even through air and guys running around in their underwear there are issues that come about and players are not on the same page and they're all learning a new system simultaneously which is what Dart acknowledged. But the silver lining in all of this without neighbors and slate in the equation is it gives these other receivers a chance to move up on the depth chart and run with the first team consistently. So Dart at least gets an idea and you can have this takeaway, Matt, even though you're not in full pads and it's not contact where you can get an idea. Okay, where does this receiver like the ball? What are the routes he's most comfortable with? I would agree this is the time of the year where that can at least help establish chemistry. I wouldn't go so far to say that it's going to be rolled over to the regular season, but I do think that there are some teachable points and routines that can be built around this time of the year. >> 100%. I mean, this is the first time that Jackson Dart is getting to throw to these pass catchers in a live setting. as you mentioned, it's not, you know, 100% like a normal game situation, but up to this point of the offseason, it's the closest thing that this team has gotten to that >> by far. >> Uh, the only other time that they really were able to do anything even close to this was that 3-day mini camp at the beginning of the offseason workout program that the Giants got because of hiring a new head coach. And but at this point, that was a month and a half ago. >> And the offense wasn't fully established. and the defense. Think about how much time has passed since then. >> Yeah, for sure. Not to mention the rookies are now integrated into the onto into into practice that obviously were not even a part of the team in early April. So, yeah, this is step one for Jackson being able to really develop that chemistry. Now, obviously, there's two more weeks of OTAAS, three days of mini camp in June. I'm sure, you know, Jackson mentioned in his press conference on Thursday that they will have some sort of, you know, organized gathering somewhere workouts where he will meet with the pass catchers and they'll, you know, run routes and do that. He, you know, he mentioned that they already did, I think, one of them in California. There will be more during that, you know, dead period between mini camp and training camp starting >> that Mooney took part in, by the way, cuz Mooney spoke about that and he's one of those new white outs. >> Yeah. And then obviously the goal is to you know when the team begins training camp when that that first practice they hit the field in West Virginia it's all you know systems firing on all on all parts you know that they want to just be able to hit the ground running and have this offense obviously a new offense new for everybody you know Mooney is actually probably the most experienced in this offense because of his previous experience with Matt Naggie but you know the goal is to try to once that comes and that day comes at the end of July get this thing going as quickly as possible because I mean obviously it's been a blink of an eye and we're already in week two of OTAAS. Another blink and we're going to be at training camp and then you know the start of the season is going to be here. So getting everyone in the offense up to speed as quickly as possible is you know probably the biggest priority for this time of year. It's interesting you phrased it that way, Matt, because I chuckled when I was listening to what Andrew Thomas had to say. And he was asked about bringing in CC Maui Noah, their new offensive lineman. And he talked about his physicality and how he's a smart player, good football IQ, all the typical compliments that you usually hear from veterans when they get their eyes and hands on a rookie. And one of the things Thomas mentioned is normally around this time of the year when you have consistency on the coaching front, the veterans are able to teach the rookies about the system because they're ahead of the curve, right? What's happening now, especially on the offensive line, they're all learning simultaneously. So, not to say that Andrew Thomas and the vets can't give valuable lessons to Maui Noah, but they're all digesting this together, which normally is not the case. Normally, right, the veterans have a few years established on the young offensive lineman or a wide receiver, quarterback, however you want to word it, it goes down the line. So that gives a little bit more on the plate of the veterans and even Jackson Dart specifically that even though it's year two and he's had a full year of NFL experience, it's new terminology as you got into and it's a new system. Even Mooney, who I would agree with you, probably is ahead of everybody else. He even said, "Listen, I played with Naggie several years ago. A number of seasons have gone by where he said it's similar, but Matt has also expanded the playbook, right? Because he's gone on to different stops. Specifically, he went back to Kansas City and worked with Mahomes. So, there are some new tricks that he has up his sleeve that he's added that is different. So, everybody is playing catchup, I would argue, but Mooney does at least have some establishment compared to the other players. Even guys likely just because they came over with Harbaugh, Greg Roman's not the offensive coordinator. So they also need to start from scratch. So that's why the OTAA period for these teams with new coaches and new systems helps to at least simulate some things in a football setting to help them, to your point, get into training camp. and you could try to start things up as fast as humanly possible. >> Yeah. I mean, for all the talk of, you know, coach bringing over all these former Ravens with him, like there's only so much that those guys can, you know, share with their new teammates because it's a new offense. It's a new defense. Guys that have never run the systems before under Harbaugh. Obviously, Donard Wilson was a defensive coordinator with the Titans and did coach under John Harbaugh in Baltimore, but he wasn't the defensive coordinator there. He wasn't calling the plays. So, it's new for everyone. Uh, so yeah, again, those former Ravens, they can, you know, at this point, the offseason workout program has already been going on for like a month and a half. So, I feel like the guys on the team now know how like Harbo runs his practices, but I mean, there's only so much that those guys can really share with their new teammates. I'm sure they will, you know, kind of get the rest of the team prepared for the start of training camp and what training camp under John Harbaugh will be like because I'm sure that will have a lot of similarities to the 18 years he was in Baltimore. But in terms of the offensive playbook and defensive playbook, this is just about everyone kind of starting from, you know, ground level. So the as many reps as possible that these guys can get together, the better it will be. So again, once the team gets together for training camp in West Virginia, everyone is just ready to hit the ground running and really gear up for the start of the season. >> On a related note to what you were just talking about, Javon Holland also spoke with reporters and he was in Miami and he has had experience with many different defensive coordinators over the stages of what has been a relatively short career. So, one of his seasons in Miami, Anthony Weaver was the defensive coordinator who clearly was also in Baltimore. So, he mentioned some of the language is similar to what Dinard Wilson is teaching because they're both from the Harbor Baltimore tree. But once again, still a lot of differences. But he did add that, and this was a question that was posed his way. You don't see this always where a former defensive back is the defensive coordinator. you know, sometimes it's maybe a non-player or a defensive lineman or a linebacker. The Giants have a former DB. And Holland said it's helpful from the standpoint of if there are things pertaining to the secondary, you go straight to the defensive coordinator to clarify things. Whereas with other setups, sometimes they're going to the DB coach or somebody else vice versa to help make sure that everybody is on the same page. those dynamics were at least a little bit interesting to hear. So, we talked about Neighbors, we talked about Slate, and the only other injury takeaway from what Harbaugh discussed was Andrew Thomas. Now, he's dealing with a shoulder injury from last season that Thomas himself acknowledged has been lingering, but he said he thinks he's in quote a good place end quote. Then, he's also addressing his foot. Now, that stems from the LizFrank injury that cut short his 2024 season, but he simply referred to it as maintenance. Mainly that they don't want him to overdo it. And this Matt has really been the game plan for Andrew Thomas for the last several seasons where no matter who the coach has been, we're going to take it easy with him. We're not going to run him into the ground because we want to make sure he's ready to go in training camp. But also there is a distinct difference in fairness compared to last year at this time where he was walking around and wearing a boot. So let's not lose sight of that. Meaning you were talking about the national media taking the neighbors information and maybe getting a little overkill. Nobody I don't think is doing that with Thomas because Thomas also acknowledged he's already taken part in some OTAAS. But whenever you hear shoulder issue, foot issue, and lingering, right, that does tend to get some people nervous. I don't think this is alarming news. I think it's refreshing, by the way, to hear players be upfront and not try to keep this stuff close to the vest and say, "Hey, listen. I'm getting some maintenance work during OTAAS. Not the end of the world. We're just trying to be smart." But it goes back to, and we've had conversations on various shows when you talk about the offensive line and who's most valuable. Yeah. they can least afford to lose, of course, their left tackle. Not to say that they don't have an option to move over there, but the dynamics completely change when you take Andrew Thomas out of the equation. And Matt, we've seen that up close and personal in previous years when they've actually lived that out in reality. So, this is not once again anything for the fan base to get nervous about, but it just goes to show you the severity of at least the foot injury that he suffered in 2024. And Alysiz Frank is a serious injury. You can't ask any player that's gone through that. You're not out of the woods simply a year later. There is still things that you have to go through to make sure there's not going to be any setbacks. >> Yeah, he wasn't on the field for Thursday's practice, which obviously was the first one in front of all the beat reporters, in front of the media, but as he mentioned, as coach mentioned, he did participate in practice earlier in the week. It's not like he has not been out there at all this spring. So, you know, they clearly have a I don't know if you want to call it a maintenance schedule, but they have a >> game plan. >> Yeah, they have a game plan for him for the spring. I'm sure it'll continue to some degree in training camp. The goal is to have him on the field ready to go at 100% health for week one. Everything before that doesn't really matter to be honest. We've seen what Andrew Thomas can do. When he is healthy and on the field, he is one of the best left tackles in the entire NFL. So, the Giants are clearly going to do everything they possibly can to make sure that when they step on the field for that Sunday night game against the Cowboys in week one, Andrew Thomas is on the field and 100% healthy. He doesn't need the same amount of, you know, ramp up and practice reps, I would say, as some of the other offensive linemen probably do. You know, that's no disrespect to them. It's just Andrew Thomas, again, when healthy is one of the best at his position. The other guys, you know, not quite to that same level. I mean, Andrew Thomas is a former allp pro, so I would not be alarmed at all about this. Again, as long as he gets, you know, some work over these next couple of weeks, stays healthy, no setbacks, when we get to training camp at the end of July, obviously that's two months away. You would think that he would be even closer, if not already, at 100% health. But even then, don't be alarmed if he sees some, you know, some days where he's not on the practice field because, again, all that matters is getting him ready to go for week one. One last thing I wanted to touch on on the non-injury front. Just listening to Jackson Dart and what he discussed. There were a lot of questions about what he's been focusing on this off season. He acknowledged about nutrition being a focus and trying to get a little bit stronger, which is natural for any young quarterback. >> You could see it. His arms significant. >> Well, and that's why specifically he was asked about that and body fat and the percentages. Listen, he was upfront and said when you get to the NFL, there's a lot of resources that are at your disposal, Matt, that you don't necessarily have even at the collegiate level. So, you get your hands on trainers or people within the building and the staff and they put you on a diet to maintain what you want to accomplish. But on the football side of things, he also got into some of the conversations that he's had with Brian Callahan. the quarterback's coach said that Callahan has been showing him a lot of film of other quarterbacks, veterans, and takeaways, things that those quarterbacks do in the pocket, how they operate. And then of course the running aspect, knowing when to slide and to not have to overdo it and take hits and the involvement of Greg Roman who I brought up, senior offensive assistant who's going to be heavily involved in the run game, of course, based on his pedigree and what he's done with San Francisco and Baltimore and the Chargers and so forth. He also had mentioned an emphasis of being under center a little bit more. So, you could tell with all of these offensive minds and what's the common element, Matt, with Roman and Callahan and Naggie? Well, they've all been offensive coordinators. You got three OC's together. And Harbo even talked about this in previous press conferences. There is going to be a process for those three individuals to come together and fine-tune the offensive system. Meaning, it's not simply Matt Naggie bringing over what he learned from Andy Reid in Kansas City and then them saying, "Okay, we're done. everybody go your separate ways. It's going to have a little Roman flavor. There may be some Callahan ideas. Naggi's taking all of this and really fine-tuning and creating, I would say, a new system from scratch almost. There is somewhat of a foundation, but he's balling up everything and trying to take a little piece of the pie from all of these individuals. So there is going to be a process for Dart and you know the onus falls on him Matt more so than any other player to get a good grasp of all of the nuts and bolts of this system so that he can pass it on to the receivers that he's working with because Andrew Thomas had said the difference he noticed out of Dart just through OTAAS is Dart's been I hate the cliché is about he's been more of a vocal leader. That's not what Andrew Thomas was getting at, but he's been more vocal on the field where he goes to receivers and he says, "Hey, I need you in this spot for this play." Not to say that that wasn't happening last season, but you could tell when you're a little bit more comfortable with the speed of the NFL and what it entails, then you're more comfortable passing that on to teammates and working on what I like to call the fine-tune nuances of the game. So that was interesting to hear what Andrew Thomas has already picked up in terms of the slight difference out of Dart. >> Yeah, I think you know for this time of year that is something that you really hope that your quarterback going into his second year that showed a lot of encouraging and promising signs as a rookie that he shows those characteristics this time of year because obviously again as we you know we can talk all as much as we want about what's going on on the field and stuff but these are spring practices. There's no contact allowed. like you got to take everything with a little bit of a grain of salt, but >> a tiny grain of salt. >> But but go ahead, please. >> Jackson's, you know, I I don't know, attitude, mindset, you know, helping trying to get everyone on the offense on the same page. That is, I would say, a big check mark for this time of year that you want to see that secondyear quarterback show. Uh I mean, you mentioned this coaching staff. There's a lot of experience, a lot. This is not just going to be, you know, the Matt Naggie from Chicago's offense or, you know, a shades of Andy like Andy Reid's offense with the Chiefs. Like, this is going to be what we've seen from the Chiefs the last few years. What we've seen from, you know, the Chargers re in recent years. Yep. >> Uh, the Titans the last couple years. And let's not forget even Tim Kelly was the interimm offensive coordinator for the Giants just last season. So, there's a lot of experience on this coaching staff. Hopefully that will benefit Jackson and his, you know, hopeful growth and development in year two. Yeah, it's just at this time of year, you want to get This is going to be a brand new offense, one that no one has ever seen before. None of these players have ever seen before. And I'm going to keep harping on this, but the main goal that you want to see out of these next few weeks is everyone being on the same page. that I think matters more than, you know, nice catches on the field or, you know, plays being made is making sure that everyone is, you know, where they're supposed to be on on a play-by-play basis. Getting a firm grasp of the playbook. I think that's got I mean, right, for this time of year, that's priority number one.
