Uh I feel like the reason why this team's been super successful, there's a lot of like-minded guys. whether it's him, whether it's myself, whether it's Jordan, uh whether it's Lane, um Zack, the list goes on and on. Um of guys who just have the will of wanting to get better and wanting to learn and improve. And you know, I see the same thing from him that I see from Jordan, that I see from Smitty. Um you, you know, even some of the coaches been in different systems before, got to adjust to this. That's what it's all about. Um you got to have the will to learn and the will to improve. And by any means, you know, I think we all could agree. Jaylen has that. How do you feel about the last one? We got coming down. >> At age 29, entering year nine, what perspective do you have of how to be effective at this point in your career? >> Um yeah, I think um I'm a big believer you put the work in and the work going to take care of itself. Doesn't mean it's going to guarantee you anything. Um I think I've spoken that before. I had to learn the hard way um when I was younger that if you just work hard, you're going to have a great year. If you just work hard um you're going to have this amount of yards and this amount of accolades and be a chance to win a Super Bowl. That just it doesn't work like that. But um even though it doesn't guarantee you anything, it gives you a hell of a chance. So I'm always going to have the the mindset of putting the work in. Um whether it's physically or mentally, um whether it's strength, whether it's speed, um mobility, um all little things that I need to improve at as a player. Um you know, I'm going have that that same mindset whether I'm 29, when I'm 21, or if I'm 33. Uh just as I got older, I just became a little more disciplined and consistent in it. >> Thanks everybody. Thank you guys. Good seeing you. Hello. We back. Let's go. You guys got got to watch practice today. I don't usually see you out there. That's cool. >> Zach, what's this going to be like for you? Obviously, you spent time in this system without Nico being when he was hurt, but obviously he was a great leader as well, just like you. What do you see as far as leadership growth even more when when the Kobe leaves like that? >> Yeah. Uh, first off, it it it hurt to see him leave, but I'm I'm happy to to watch him go, and he I know he's going to succeed wherever he is. He taught me I I thank him from the bottom of my heart for um from when I came here to learn the system, to teach me about how to play inside linebacker. Um that's my brother and um I wish him the the the best. But as far as as this team and now in terms of a leaders leadership aspect, um I feel like we have a lot of guys that can take over leadership. Um obviously he was a big part. Um but we have a lot of guys Jordan Davis um myself, Cooper Cooper Deene, Quinan Mitchell. Um all the starters can take ownership in that in that leadership in the locker room on the field and take charge um just as Nico did. I know Jad is re rehabbing, but based on what you saw through last season and some of the growth that he he showed, how ready do you feel like he is to step into this? >> Yeah, super excited for him. Um, obviously going through the rehab process um and getting back out on the field. But it's been cool. It's been really cool um thinking about how now I'm the veteran teaching the younger guy and um little things like I I quick story about Jiad. Last year, week one, we had install meeting. And if you've never been, obviously you guys haven't been in an install meeting with Vic, but um it's intense. It's a lot of information all at one time. And Jiad hadn't had that yet. Um he was sitting right next to me. I was watching him glimp glimpse at him take notes and on a on a notebook, chicken scratch with a pencil. Um and right after the meeting, we go to individual meetings. I said, "Jiad, let me see your notes and take a look." I'm like, "Yeah, go upstairs, talk to Pat, get yourself an iPad, a pen, um, and this is how we're going to do it." And just teaching small things like that, I think, uh, are are really in influential to him and his growth and development. And you saw growth through all throughout the season. So, I'm really excited for him um, this upcoming >> You mentioned Vic there, year three with you. Uh, how much have you grown with his defense from when you first got here? >> Yeah. uh obviously a lot and I've grown a lot as a player especially in this scheme but um learning where I can make plays, where are the weaknesses of of the defense, who's dropping where, who to communicate to. Um if communication needs to go from a safety down to an outside backer, um if it's not clear or I don't hear it, um I'll make sure that Dline gets that that communication. So being able to implement myself in ways that um is outside of my position in my realm is is really been cool. >> Jean is up a bit like >> Yeah, he's swole. He's swole. Um I mean he was he was big before too, but um he's working. He's grinding. He's he's doing his best cuz um when when you're at your best um when when you have when you're coming off a Pro Bowl year and all pro year, you have to do your best to um you have to try even harder the following year. So, he's working his tail off um to to to be better, which is crazy to think about. >> What stood out to you um two of the defensive additions, Tyreek Pullman and Jonathan Bernard coming recently. What your early impressions of those guys being around stood out to you? Yeah, super excited about those additions. Um, Reek the Fry. I remember seeing him. I was training here in the offseason. I remember seeing him when he came into sign. I'm like, that that guy's tall. Like he's like a true 6'4. Dang near feels like 6'6. Um, lengthy lanky dude, super fast, super smooth. Watching him work out is is incredible. Um, and the things he can do on the field, his attitude, I think it'll fit really well for this defense. And then Jonathan Gernard, I I knew him. He was my draft class. um knew him through combine and and and training and all that. Um so it was cool to be united with him and I know the things he can do on the field and the things he can bring this defense. I'm super excited. >> You mentioned helping the younger guys offense that people have now you've played against you know the the Rams, the Packers, the Ners, what challenges does it present in linebacker? Yeah, I in my head even just practicing and having played against those teams, um I feel like all the challenges are on the linebackers. The way things are crossing in front of your face, the condensed formations, even down to the way the offensive line is is trained to to attack the linebackers and um it it's truly they're working as a unit and they're they're doing really good right now picking it up. Um I'm really excited for for our offense. When you talk about your comfort level with another year in this defense, how does that show up on the field? Like what are the things that you might notice now that you didn't notice a couple years ago? Yeah, I feel like I'm worried less now about what my responsibility is and can really hone in on into what the offense is doing and uh preparing that way. But also um continuing to find the ways I can steal plays if I can jump into this window and make an interception or or tip a ball, get a PBU. Um I'm finding doing my best to find those those ways, too. We were talking to D earlier um last week he was he was saying that he told you guys that you he called it like he was reverse aging and I'm just curious in year three what what do you see from him from that? Do do you remember that conversation? What's what's he what's he like in year three? >> He uh he says he's reverse aging. I know that's by the blood work and all that stuff. >> That's funny. Um same old guy. same guy um bringing I feel like he's um taking things to the next level this year um in terms of he knows we're comfortable and he knows we know our scheme and what he knows us and he knows what we're we're capable of from a knowledge aspect. So um I I I think it's cool that he even within his own scheme he continues to develop and tweak and change and um especially to the personnel. It was heard that he was pondering retirement this offseason. I'm curious how that works with you guys. Does he communicate anything to you? Are you trying to convince him to come back? What was that like? >> Uh I I the past two years I' towards the end of the season I've sent subtle nudges like coming back again, coming back again, but it's it's up to his decision, his discretion. Um he's been coaching this league for a really long time and um only he will know when his time is right to retire. You know, it's very interesting you say that because when he in other stops there had been bit of a reputation that he could be really difficult in term and really challenging is probably a better way to say it and some players didn't respond to that. Seems like you guys have you've been feeling this for >> I have my I don't I don't know the the real answer, but I feel like our defense is so young. um we're one of the youngest defenses in the league and a lot of guys went to school like at Georgia and Alabama and um these big-time schools where the coaches were were tough and hard and even myself going to Wisconsin like um and when you're fresh out of out of college and you're used to that mentality um and and and that's what Vic is. He's a hard-nosed old school football coach that um if you're willing to learn and and listen to um what he has to say, not always the tone in his voice, but what he has to say, um it could be really good for you. And I think it's been really good for this defense. >> We haven't spoken to you since the end of last season, but it seems like on that that play against the 49ers, the fake uh in the Hard Knocks video afterwards, you were you were blaming yourself for it. um was that your responsibility? Is that a play that you look back upon um with regret? And what does that teach you about accountability after becoming a captain for the first time? >> Yeah, a play like that in the past for me um would have destroyed me. Uh I would have been super down in the dumps and I would have played worse. Um but the the game is about ownership. I I messed up. We were in man. I had the back. Um yes, it was a trick play, but no excuse. and you learn from it and and you you take your hits and keep rolling. >> That's it. >> Thanks, guys. >> The man. Thank you. >> All right. >> Great to see y'all at OTAAS. Let's get started. >> Do you feel any different um this year versus previous ones coming off the extension? >> I would say so. Um, every year really looking forward to finding a new thing to get better at, whether that's technique, um, film watching, just understanding the game on a different level. So, definitely that's been a more thing that I have been locking in on. Um, it's an exciting process to learn. OTAAS is the time to learn new things. So, um, we've been doing new things in the Dline room. I know instead of playing those, getting a little three reps, but you know, it's just little improvement like that. What are your early impressions of who are >> He's a good guy, great guy. Um, he's really meshing into the room well. Um, and not that we had any reservations or doubt that he wouldn't, but just seeing him flourish in the room and seeing him get connected with the guys. Um, and especially because of Moro Jumbo, obviously we all know that he's Nigerian as well. And just having that connection in that room, it's probably paying dividends in itself. But just getting to know him, getting him getting to know us, uh, understanding that he's learning a new sport. I mean, when I started playing football in 10th grade, it was already hard enough. And I could just only imagine at his point in his career and coming into the highest level and learning in the NFL. So, um, aside from that, day by day, he gets better. Um, and obviously we all know that it's not going to happen overnight, but just seeing his progression and seeing him work and just understanding the type of humility that kid has and it's just amazing to work with. I'm excited to just work with him each day. >> What's it been like for the Georgia guys to have Makobi no longer here? >> It's a little bittersweet. Um, you know, obviously his presence is definitely missed, but at the end of the day, you know, we can only rely on the guys that we have here. So, we've been leaning on um Jal, we've been leaning on Zack, we've been leaning on Tro, we've been leaning on all the guys in the room. So, um, you know, he's gone but never forgotten. We're not going to sit there and act like he died or anything. You know, we can always see him whenever we want to. But, uh, you know, it's just having that and I think it just hits especially hard for us because we played with him for so long and, um, you have that experience and now learning into a new year and not having him behind us is uh, kind of a just a bittersweet feeling. But, you know, we know he's out there working. I know he's in Vegas doing his thing and, you know, being the same Kobe that we all know that he is. So, exciting. in the workout videos of Jaylen Carter. Um, how important is it right now? It seems like the shoulders are good unlike last all season. What what what do you expect from him this year being healthy going into the season? >> Um, I think we all know the type of player that Jaylen Carter is, the caliber of player that he had, the potential that he has. Um, you know, it's a new year. It's a new year. We all have to go out there. We all have to work. We have to go out there and prove And um I think that if everybody buys into that mentality, then we can go out there and be our best. It's not about just him. I think more so about the Dline, we're more focused on the collective unit of all getting better. Um we know Jaylen's going to add to the room. He's been doing it for years, but you know, as a collective, we were trying to figure out how to get better as a collective. Um I'm glad that he's healthy. I'm glad that he's getting his reps and he's getting his rest, but uh you know, we just got to go out there and we have to focus on the main thing. It's about us and um I know he's going to go out there and he's going to ball. So, we just have to make sure that we all do our part. >> Know it's early, but what are your early impressions of going against the offensive line with the new coaching system? >> Yeah. Yeah. So, um we got started this week against going against the offense. I'm sure y'all know that. But, um it's exciting. It's exciting. Um a lot of the things that they're doing now is what gave us troubles last year. So to be able to see it in practice and not just see it on the you know week of the game, you know, that's a lot of experience that we can take for ourselves in defense, get better at that. And um you know, as I talk to the players around and just seeing how they feel about it, they feel really good about it. So um if they like it, I love it. I can't obviously I don't know the ins and outs of all the offense and stuff like that, but you know, just looking at it from paper, looking at it from film, looks exciting. Um I love what they got going on. I'm sure they do, too. So we'll keep it at that. Last off seasonason, um, you lost a lot of weight, you were in great condition, you had a great year. How are you feeling physically you got this off >> Same. Um, right now it's about getting as strong as I can. Um, I think a lot of players have the same philosophy. They want to get stronger in the offseason and then after OTAAS, as we start wrapping up the condition, start wrapping up and start getting into football shape more. Um, but yeah, in terms of the offseason, I mean, our program, um, you know, it's challenging. That's one thing I can commend him on. Uh it's not going to be easy coming in, especially like when we go outside, we had those shuttles and stuff like that. Um and obviously, I don't know if y'all got a chance to watch the box drills and everything, but you know, that's that's that's some work in itself. So, uh you know, just going out there, it's exciting to go out there and work with the guys. Uh we all lean on each other in those times of moments because it's going to be challenging. You're going to have challenging moments in the season. So when we go out there and we attack the boss drills and we do it as a unit, we do it as a team um because the offensive during our conditioning as well, it kind of brings that bonding that we all talk about how we would need that bonded by trial, trial by fire. So um you know, we excited to get moving and um when the offseason gets or offseason, but when OTA is over with, that's when we start getting into more of the football and technique and the conditioning. Get ready for that. What's been the biggest difference for you if there is one between the two three months since signing contract? Um, >> I would say it's probably the standard that I've raised for myself, you know. Um, knowing as I, you know, I always been the oldest in the room, le at least for last year. Um, I know we got TQ, but it feels like I've been here for the longest. So, you know, it's just uh understanding that, you know, everything is starts from the head down to the toes. So, um starts with our coach, coach Clint. You know, he has a high standard for us, he has a high standard for the Dline, he has a high standard for the unit, and also having a high standard for ourselves, which also translates for the unit, having a high standard for ourselves. and you know um knowing that like you know even though you feel good about something that you can always get better and I think that's the beautiful thing about having UR with us is that you know we can see who are going through the same trials and tribulations that we have you know and I tell sometimes I'm like hey like I still get tripped up on this my footwork is still sloppy on this like you know I could always get better with that and uh you know having him it makes you want to do your reps perfectly so you can set a good example and um at least that's how I think I know Mo um by and all those guys can attest to that but We all just trying to perfect ourselves and knowing that we're never going to be perfect. But if we keep climbing, if we keep reaching for that goal, then who knows the sky's we can reach the limit. >> You had a chance to uh be a part a couple weeks ago when the girls flag championships were here. A, what did you think of what you saw and b just the growth of the sport? Any thoughts on what you've seen in that regard? >> Definitely. um hearing just the history of the teams and understanding like one of the coaches that was uh spearheading the movement for bringing girls uh competitive flag football into I want to say the state of New Jersey in Pennsylvania. Um that was pretty cool learning about that. Um seeing that how much traction they had already um the stands were filled here. Um the girls had great energy. Uh lots of resource. I seen someone with like concussion headbands. I was like okay so they they're really serious about this. But, you know, just the type of passion that they have. Like, I think uh what stuck out to me was just the drive and hunger that they had just playing against each other. I think they were all excited just to be at uh Jefferson Jefferson Health. >> It's Jefferson Health. You know, I don't want to say I don't want to say the other old name, but you know, get in trouble, but uh Jefferson Health like they came out here, they was excited. They was excited to play here and see that, you know, the guys uh, you know, just us being football players, they were excited for that. But just seeing how they went on the field, attack the field and just seeing them get mad, frustrated at the plays that they miss and I was like, man, like that translates against all sports, male, female, it doesn't matter. Um, it's just really cool just to see and just experience that. And, uh, you know, I definitely excited to see how far they go into the future. >> This is the uh, this is the second straight year you guys have had kind of like big losses on defense with guys leaving. Um what's kind of the key to like you know keeping it all together, keep the defense, you know, playing well, you know, trying to overcome like the guys who left and everything. >> Yeah, I'd say um um that's the thing about football. You're always going to have wins and losses. You're always going to lose a couple players. You're always going to gain a couple players. But, um the teams who do it well, they spend that time during this time right now connecting with their teammates, getting them up to speed. you know, we're fortunate enough to have Vic into our is this our third year with Vic? >> Third year with Vic. Wow. Time flies. Um to have our third year going in with Vic. So, you know, we understand the playbook a little bit more. Um but at the same time, it's also things to learn. It's different for us. You know, we're not quite starting at, you know, the the drawing board, but we're also trying to trick our brains into learning more things into learning the nuances of the defense, especially as a D lineman, learning the nuances of the defense that Vic throws in. And um I think that's just an important thing that uh kind of translates from year to year. Uh but you know in terms of the new players like it feels like they've been here for the longest time. So I think that's the beautiful thing about the culture that we have here the things that we try to cultivate on this side of the ball. So you know we just keep working. Um the fastest way to get connected with somebody is to work with them. So um I definitely think in the future it's going to translate. What's it been like uh to watch Clint work with you are? Um seems really exciting when they draft him in that video. And what what generally makes him a good teacher? Seems like a lot of different guys from Byron Mororrow all taking steps. What makes Clint a good developmental, you know, teacher as a coach? Um, I think Coach Hurt, to answer your first question, is just really excited to work with him because, you know, it's just a chance for him to learn a new sport, for him to get better, for him to help his family, for him to, you know, it's all the reasons off the field that we're doing it for. And, um, you can talk to, he has his why, and understanding his why, you know, it's a lot deeper than just X's and O's. And I think that's one thing that Clinton hurt and as well as myself and everybody else in that room that we understand fully. Um when we know each other's why, when we know what we're playing for, we know the drive, what drives us each day. Um that's something that you can lean on when things get hard. And so, you know, football's going to get hard. It's going to get hard during the season. I'm sure like who is going to go to a point in season where he's like, "Man, like we got 16 more weeks of this thing." And I'm like, "Yeah, like it's going to happen." But, you know, just seeing him work, just seeing him, even when he mess up, he's going to mess up. We're all bound to mess up. He gets right back to it. He gets right back to it. It's the same drive. It's the same hunger. And I think, you know, um, exes O's aside, that's just somebody that you're willing to work with, you're willing to help. So, just seeing Clint um, just walk him through and just, you know, I'm learning things, you know, along with him that, um, I wasn't expecting to learn when who I came through. So, you know, it's just really cool just to go through that process. And uh can you remind me of your second question? >> Just generally what makes him a good teacher as a defensive line coach? You know, different guys like Byron Young have developed more. What makes Clinton, you know, so effective in his role? >> He understands development and he understands from not just the D lineman perspective, but just as a defense a whole obviously we knew he was a coordinator, so he knows from the inside, the out, the top and the bottom. But um he also knows the type of person that he's dealing with. So, like when he coaches me up, he coaches me up way differently than he coaches Mo up. And it's not saying that he's like taking it easy or doing it harder on me, but it's just he knows the type of person that we are. He knows what makes us tick. He knows, you know, he's spent time enough with us just to learn the type of people that we are and how we respond to different coaching. And um I think that's just one thing, you know, he always he's going to get the most out of you, but he's not just going to be like rah rah, like you know, this is what you got to do, blah blah blah, and that's that. He's also giving you a ear. He's letting you explain yourself why you did a certain player or why did you make a certain call or why did you do this instead of doing that? He understands that we're not robots, we're athletes and you know he works with that. If we did something wrong, we'll fix it. But at the end of the day, he cares about our effort. He cares about how hard we go and he cares about just the drive that we have. And after that, we can fix everything else. And I think that's the mindset that we all have. >> All right. Thanks everybody. >> Appreciate y'all.

title: Nick Sirianni On Team's Progression Through OTAs
text: All right. How we doing? >> How about it? And >> you've seen Jaylen go through a lot of offensive coordinators, a lot of play callers. What have you noticed about how he handles that? >> Yeah, again, I think Jaylen, one thing that's really special about Jaylen is just how consistent he is with his approach to getting better every single day. um regardless of, you know, if we're calling a concept one thing or we're calling a concept another thing or who the the play caller is, um or who his quarterback coach is, just just consistency from Jaylen, um with how he approaches a daily process and that that and you always I always admire that about him. >> Nick, Nolan Smith was pulled over for speeding. Did you address that with him and what's your overall message to the team? Yeah, obviously. Um, any any conversation I have with any player will always stay private. Um, with that being said, we address everything. Um, we talk about everything. We talk when when it's appropriate to talk about it with the individual, we talk about it with the individual. When it's appropriate, uh, to discuss it as a team, you know, I I'll choose to discuss it as a team. So, um, so yeah, it's important. Obviously, what's so important is that we learn from our mistakes and and we not only on the football field, but in the, you know, in the community as well, and we try to get better from those those things. And everything that we go through is a teachable moment um on the field, off the field. Um and that's a big part of of getting better. Um and so, like I said, everything we address um it's just a matter of how we do that um with our players. But that's why it's so important that you're in constant communication with your players. Have good relationships with your players. Um, not that every conversation is going to be, hey, loveydovey, right? There's there's hard conversations, there's tough conversations, there's conversations where you laugh, there's conversations where you cry, there's conversations where, you know, you go through a process of that. So, uh, yeah, >> Sean, uh, mentioned sort of a blend of the offense and you mentioned that with some of the things Jaylen has done well, when you went through this with with Kellen, do you lean on that when you went through it before? >> Sure. Again, it's about the best situation that we can put the players of the Philadelphia Eagles in and what what what is our scheme going to be as a Philadelphia Eagles? Um, and I think that that changes year in year out, whether it's the same coordinator or you promote from within or if you go from the outside. Um, and so we're always doing what we think we need to do to help our players be put them in the best positions to succeed, to do what they do well. Um, and Sean's done an awesome job uh thus far and and just really um like the command that he has uh in front of the room and the conviction that he has in front of the room and the knowledge that he has in front of the room. Um and so yeah, we'll see how that looks. We got a long time before we play. We got a lot of practice to go through before we we play a game. This is about, you know, figuring out what we do well, what we can what we can do well, and and sharpening our tools that, you know, you can run any scheme you want, but if you can't block, if you can't catch, if you can't protect the football, it doesn't it doesn't really matter. So, all those things that aren't looked at as sexy, right? The dirty work stuff. Um, that's what we're working on perfecting right now as we get to to know some new terminology and some new things, the way the offense goes. And for that matter, the new some of the new things, you know, um what I love about Coach Fangio is like Coach Fangio has continued to evolve his uh as a as a coordinator um throughout his entire career and the new things that he's that he's doing. Um you know, it's it's never the the same year in year out. So, um that's what we're working on right now. >> Nick, none of your O linemen, your starting O linemen have ever had a different position coach than Stout. What have you seen from from Chris Cooper as far as winning those guys over and kind of establishing himself? >> Yeah, I don't think again it's not about the win over. It's about it's about daily doing what your job is supposed to be and that and that's the players doing that with Chris uh and to us as a coaching staff and us as coaches doing that with them. you're constantly putting deposits in the bank um by building trust by you know your knowledge, your conviction, uh daily daily um daily work. Um and that's what we're working on right now is is is that um you know and that's on both ends like these guys have to build trust with him and he's got to build trust with them. It's not a one-way street and it never is. Um and so that's what we're working on right now. Uh, but I love the way Chris comes to I I've been with offensive line for the last 5 years. I love how they come to work and uh with an attempt to get better every single day. And then the same thing on Chris's part. Uh great knowledge for the game, great ability to connect with players. Um you know, great knowledge of the scheme of different types of things that we're going to be doing. Um and then just great growth mindset to to figure out things that that he may have not has not done in the past. So, um, that's what we're working on at this at this particular moment and that's what's going on. >> To follow up on on Rub's question, like how much of a learning process is it for like a lot of the offensive linemen considering they've only had pretty much one way under Stalin before now? >> Yeah. Again, there's a there's a learning process for what's important that regardless of carryover, regardless of everything. What's important that everyone needs to do at this time of year is start back at square one and build our habits again from square one. We do that with our fundamentals. We do that with our schemes. Uh we do that with our core values. And so everybody is and that's what we've tried to do throughout the the five years. We don't just because you've been together, the offense has been the same or the defense has been the same, that doesn't mean you just assume that everyone's at phase four of where they need to be. Um, no, you start back at square one. You start back at the little minute details. Um, because we all need reminded on that. Like shoot, I'll be I'll be giving the similar messages messages all year because it's the relentlessness of it's the relentless approach of the things that you believe in that you need to do on a daily basis. And um and so that's where we're at right now is uh everybody starting at square one um because that's kind of how we go about our offseason program. >> With square one, I mean Mark Bell, rookie coming in. What does he look like at this point? And I know you guys value the mentorship. Um the chance to be out there guys like Lane and Jordan, but what what does he look like? >> Yeah, again he he's just going through uh the process, you know, again, we don't have pads on right yet. Obviously, a big part of the evaluation offensive lineman and for that matter any position, it's football, right? Um you see how laser focused I was into that distraction. Um, and that's sure as heck a statement for an offensive lineman who really has to go with the physicality of of of things that has to happen when they play. Um, but it's about those little things, the mental portion of it. I think he's really sharp mentally of being able to pick things up. You know, it seems like he's learning something new every day and, you know, handles the volume that has been thrown at him in a very positive manner. And so, um, and you like the ability that he has to move and his obvious, uh, freakish size, uh, when he's out there. So, he's had good drills and and done really well in drills, has done really well, uh, in the classroom, and we look to for him to continue to develop in that. But, nobody's a finished product right now, as you guys know. I I know you guys know that, like, nobody's a finished product. And we're and we're very early on in the stages of this. Um, you know, we're going to make mistakes out there at practice today as players. we're going to make mistakes out there as practice coaches. Um, but the mindset has to constantly be is like, okay, made a mistake today. Um, you should be hungry for that and be understand how much you can improve on every mistake that you make um or and for that matter every positive thing that you do. And so this is a long long process that um we're being diligent about every single day to to continue to get better. I know it's like, oh, that's coach speak. And that's just really how we live and how we go about our business uh of just staying locked into the present. >> What have you seen in the growing relationship between Shawn and Jaylen and and your relationship with Sean as well? >> Yeah. Trust is built through daily showing up and doing what you're supposed to do, right? Um and and so it takes time. Um and you know, I like I said, I admire what I admire about Jaylen is just his one of the things I admire about Jaylen is the you know, his commitment to get better uh every single day and his commitment to the process. And when you do that, you build that trust with with people. Um, and Sean, man, Sean's here at all hours of the day. Uh, I'm not sure I've beat Shawn in here yet this year. And I'm not sure I've left earlier than him or I've always left earlier than him uh to this point. like he is he grinds and he does what he's supposed to do and and works really hard at his craft and and so like you admire that but that takes time and that's and that's built and so that's what we're working on right now. Again, all this is a is a process I think and I understand you guys questions because it's like I haven't talked to you in a while. Let me ask some of these questions and and I guess my answer to most of them has been well it's a process. It's a process. It is not I'm not trying to give you guys just coach speak. It's just the way way it is. But um we talk about that trust a lot of how that's built and uh those are really you know the hardships uh the time that you spend and const and consistently doing what you're supposed to do is what builds those things. So you know and those guys don't miss you know Sean and Jaylen what I admire about them is they don't miss a day on that. So, whatever day we're on right now, 50, I don't think it's that high, but 30, whatever, uh, is that that's how far along we are in the relationship? Because I'm not sure that either of those guys have missed a day where they've, you know, of of doing what they're supposed to do because of who they are. >> Has Dvonte's attendance been any different this spring than previous years might? >> I'd have to look there. Uh we've had what I'm excited about of the attendance that we've had of the guys uh that have been here and uh excited to work with the guys at this point of this the season and but I would have to go back Jeff and look at that and uh but you know I know this about Devonte every day he's here he's working his butt

title: Milton Williams & Andy Borregales Address the Media | Patriots Press Conference
text: Good to be back. >> Yeah. Yeah, sir. >> How uh how was it out there for you guys today? >> No, we got some good work. Um same as last year. You know, we ain't out there just playing around. We we really getting some work in and um you know, getting new guys acclimated, you know, learning some new things. Um but pushing each other the same way. What's the most important thing for you to focus on this time of year? >> Um, technique because you really, like you said, we ain't got no pads on, so it's not as physical as, you know, some of players want it to be. Um, there's a lot of tech technical things and just being in condition. That's um things you can focus on the most right now. >> Milton, how do you uh look at this time of year and how important is it to the team building process? Yeah, it's early early in the year, but also like I said, um new systems, new things going in for, you know, new players coming in, you know, just starting that getting that camaraderie early on, you know, it's just going to help us in the long run like it did last year. >> Milton, you come off a Super Bowl winning year and then a Super Bowl runner up year back to back. What does this team need to do to take that lift? >> Man, we was on the doorstep last year. I don't feel like we really need to change up much. Um, obviously we had a lot of younger players just getting that experience and learning and growing from from the mistakes that we made last year. Um, I feel like everybody can can just continue to get better and if we all get better, you know, maybe we'll make that that one or two plays that that hurt us. >> How did you process that loss? And, you know, does that add any anything extra for you this off season? >> Uh, no. I mean, now we went out there and fought. Um, it was a long year. you know, guys playing through injury. Um, like I said, but we we still went out there and fought and, you know, try to get a win. Ultimately, we didn't get it done. So, you know, hold your head and get back to work and let's fight for it again this year. >> With that in mind, are you excited, anxious about the possibility of facing the uh the Seahawks? >> I mean, Super Bowl in the regular season, that's different thing. But, you know, whoever we play, I don't I don't care who we play, you know, I'm I'm ready for the challenge. >> Working with more. Obviously, last year we saw you guys had a lot of chemistry working together, but how has that, if any, if at all grown now going into this like second year of getting to work with him? >> Yeah, we're just competing every day, competing with each other, holding each other accountable. Like I always we always tell each other, you know, this team and this defense going to go as far as we take them. you know, if we control a lot of the scrimmage up front, you know, it help our team in in a lot of ways defensively and offensively. But, um, like I said, we just showing up every day trying to be a good example, uh, for the younger guys and, you know, keep building. >> NFL released a survey saying that 92% of players preferred grass over artificial turf. I'm just curious, what is the biggest difference on playing on grass versus turf for you? I feel like um just grass. I feel like you your cleats come out come in and out better. I feel like you you can cut more or cut better. Um but I do like playing on some turfs like New Orleans turf. I think they got the best turf in the league. So I like playing in that stadium. Do you have to resist putting on your general manager's hat and going upstairs and saying trade uh trade for AJ Brown because I was a teammate with him in Philadelphia? >> Definitely. Um and now you you see the noise and you see it. Um shoot hell of a player. He he can definitely you know help our team. But you know that down pay me to do that. >> What was what kind of teammate was he like? What was it like to be around him? >> Uh great dude. you know, monster on the field, great in the locker room, you know, holding guys accountable and holding himself accountable. Um, I feel like that's everything you want in a in a player of his caliber. >> A lot of times, um, players who have won lost championships say that they the loss kind of sticks with them more than than the win does. They think about that a little bit more. having done that the last two years. Is that the way your off season was as well where that that stuck a little more than the wind did? >> Definitely because um you always just think about the plays that you miss or the plays that you know you could have capitalize on that just stick with you forever. I remember plays from my first couple years in the league that I could have made and um but on a big stage like that, you know, not getting a job done. Um, you just kind of replay those plays in your mind. Wake up in the middle of the night thinking about it. Um, but it's just fuel for the for the next day and, you know, wake up and figure out what we're going to get better at today and, uh, when that time comes, be ready. >> You guys um, didn't have Christian Gonzalez out there practice today. What do you guys miss when he's not around? >> No, he one of the best corners in the league. So, uh, he a big piece of our team and our defense. Um, I'm pretty sure he'll be back, but like I said, they don't pay me to make the calls like that. >> Coach Brael, he >> last question. >> Is he the same guy he's always been? And if he is, do you appreciate that? >> Yeah, same guy talking, you know, getting guys, you know, ready to roll. You know, he he ain't he ain't change one bit. How you guys doing? >> So, first off, did you have any impact in Bryce also adopting a dog? Because I know that you got one LA or was it last year at training camp, right? And then he got one at like his last event. Did you have anything? Were you at all influential in that decision? >> Um, you know, me and Bryce, we were kind of pushing Julian to get that dog. >> Julian, sorry. >> No, it's all right. Um, you know, he's always been on the fence of getting a dog, but here we are and now he has Mel. It was Maple before, but changed it to Maple. And I'm like, "All right, cool." >> Andy, you don't have any, you know, direct competition this summer, but how you sort of, I guess, for lack of a better term, stay involved and sort of mentally keep yourself, you know, locked in. >> Um, really just trying to be better than the day before. just every day try to, you know, get give myself a challenge just to be better. Um, I kind of tell myself like even though I may not be in a competition, um, I'm in a competition with myself. Um, and just kind of keep that, I guess, hunger mentality just to keep, you know, striving to get better. >> We talked to some of the other guys about what they thought when they saw Seattle on the schedule, the opener regular season. There's a level of excitement, I imagine, too. But Drake also talked about the fact chance to get back in a team. You left a bad taste of your mouth. >> What where do you stand with that? >> Um I mean same stance. I mean I'm excited um just to get out there and then especially with with all the new guys. I mean we we've all kind of grown together very quickly and you know I'm excited for for what's to come. >> What you look back on last year, what did you learn from it? Did you thought through the offseason? How much better can you be or try to be this this year? Um, I mean I learned a lot. There was there's so many things that that I learned that I probably could sit here for two hours, however long. Um, but I mean the biggest thing is is really um don't get too low, don't get too high and just stay neutral. Like you're going to have big moments, you're going to have low moments at the end of the day. That's all part of the game. Just keep moving forward. What are the biggest things that you're looking to personally get out of OTAAS as a kicker? And when it comes to the team building aspect of things, how does that dynamic kind of work here in OTA? >> Um, I mean, as a kicker, it's it's really just making sure my ball flight's good and obviously we still have a good bit of time until the season comes. So, it's not like I have to be 100% perfect every day, but that's what I'm striving for. Um, and honestly just any little thing that that may need to be tweaked like tweak it now so I'm not middle of a game trying to switch something. Um, and team aspect. I mean really it's I mean it's really a family. I mean it's not really a team in in my eyes >> since the season ended to coming back on April 20th for the start of the program. Any um what was the most exciting thing that happened? >> Uh exciting thing uh wife got pregnant. um having a boy. So that's exciting. It's probably the number one thing >> that's that's pretty high on the list. >> Yeah. >> Were you able to get away at all and like how did you sort of refresh after such a long a long >> Um yeah I mean I I went back home for for a week. Um then me and my wife went to California for a week then came back here. I went back to California uh with Bryce just to work out over there for a week. um came back here and just been here ever since. So, >> how much of a blur was season one for you from the time you got, you know, you're on the team, you're here, OTAA's training camp, you just kept going all the way through the postseason. >> Yeah, I mean it it flew by. Like sometimes it felt so slow, but I look back and I'm like that that flew by quick. Um, and like even sometimes like I catch myself like dang like I'm kind of I'm going into year two like that that was fast. Um, but just trying to take in every every day. >> Has your relationship with Jeremy Springer, Tom Quinn grown it all now that you're in your second season? >> Yeah, definitely. I mean, it's it's always been a two-way street. You know, I I always, you know, voice my opinions. They obviously coach me up. Um, and I love the the dynamic that that we have and you know, I'm looking forward to keep it going. >> You mentioned some of the experimental type of things you might do. Um, is that more to get distance, accuracy? Like what does that what does that look like when you're looking at doing something a little bit different um in OTAAS that you might not tinker with during regular season? >> Um, for me it's just accuracy um and especially just ball flight um especially like wind or or conditions and stuff like that. just making sure that that ball flight is clean enough that no matter what win, it's not going to just go one way and next thing you know the ball's 20 yards to the left or the right. Um, so just keep that ball flight just nice and straight. >> I know there's a lot of discussion among players natures here in these stadiums because of the World Cup. Where do you stand on natural grass versus turf as a kicker? >> Um, honestly I like both. Um, if I had to choose, I'd probably go grass, but I really don't mind turf. Um, especially when it gets colder, um, cuz it's a little easier to to plant in. Um, but I'm kind of good on both. So, >> how do you feel about the whole FIFA takeover? And have you gotten any chances to get some soccer games in Gillette Stadium? I know, not for FIFA, but for Legacy or for uh >> Yeah. Um, I went to the the Brazil France friendly. That was fun. Um, and then I want to say a couple weeks ago or maybe last week, went to a Revs game. Um, that was fun, too. Obviously, I'm a big soccer fan, so just being there was fun. >> You get to get tickets or you >> I'll be I'll be in Miami, so I'm trying to get tickets down there, so we'll see. >> Feel like you can challenge any of those guys competition? >> Probably. >> Yeah, I can. >> Andy, just bring you back for a second to the turf versus graph a grass question. Do you find like distance is a big difference? You were talking about planting and how you're able to plant, you think a little bit better on, you know, on one surface versus the other. What about what about kicking distance? >> Um distance the ground doesn't really affect me much unless it's like just pouring down and it's like a grass field. Like I may need to just plant a little different. Um but doesn't really affect my distance much. That's more of like temperature, wind, things like that. kind of about getting better as you in your craft. How much does the continuity of your group help uh with that? But also knowing the elements, knowing New England now, knowing what to expect when you go up there uh in certain months, certain winds and conditions like that. >> Yeah, it's it's definitely something fun that I mean obviously having Julian and Bryce um we all go through it together. Um cuz we we all have to either do something a little different depending on like the wind, the weather like you said. Um, but I mean going through it a whole year, you kind of know what to expect. Um, but then again, you kind of go in and it's like you may expect one thing and then halfway through the game, it's completely different. So, you kind of just have to adjust on the fly. >> Anything else, guys? >> All right. >> Good. >> Thanks, Andy. >> Congratulations. >> Thank you. Yeah.

title: Drake Maye: "Trying to Take It to the Next Level." | Patriots Press Conference
text: How are you? >> It's nice in here. >> You like You guys like it? >> Not too bad. >> How's yours? >> Good. Good. I like it in here. >> Did you put on weight? I'm sorry, Karen. >> Yeah. Do you need to dye it? >> No. I'm just wondering um if you feel any different coming in this year being the second year in Josh's offense and uh you know you feel more comfortable confident uh with the offense year two >> I think it's it's it's naturally it's naturally going to be more comfortable you know being in the huddle staying the play calls knowing why we're running the plays um kind of trying to take the next level of details and and details inside of each play and I think it's it's fun getting to you have new guys in the offense and me try to, you know, teach them, you know, what I know about it and what I think will be best for us to, you know, best execute. And I think it's, you know, that's what's fun, you know, being out here and maybe trying some different things, but also trying just to execute and create positive plays. So, um, it's it's nice, you know, getting another year in a new off in the same offense. Um, it's been first time for me in, you know, four maybe four years. So, um, it'll be it's great to have that and, um, have a offensive mind of Coach McDaniels and our offensive coaches are great. So, I'm really looking forward to that and you got to keep building. Follow up rude question. Are you thicker with two C's? Is that the way you're supposed to say it? Is that kind of like the hip thing? >> Are you thicker with two C's? Is that how it's supposed to be? Or >> that's paused if that's anything. I think that's a that's that's not the way to put it. But uh >> um you better do you feel condition as far as another year of experience just your body getting getting ready for this? I think that's I think that's just part of you know having a long season and be able to take some time off and come back into it and get your body right for the uh beginning of the season. I think it's kind of the how the NFL works the long season and you know you you tend to you lose some muscle or lose some way as the season goes on. You try to maintain that. That's what you try to build you know during the offseason and maintain during the season. So uh that's kind of the nature of it and just trying to you know be my my best version of myself and that's you know physically and mentally. What was your reaction to seeing the Seahawks on the schedule for week one? >> I think it's a um it's it's a chance for us to, you know, get some extra motivation during training camp, you know, with the with starting off with the bang, you know, like that. You know, a chance to get a opponent that, you know, left a bad taste in our mouth. So, I think it's, you know, something for us that's going to, you know, really make us work. You know, we got to, you know, bring it week one, you know, on the road in a tough environment, you know, with their, you know, they're going to be hanging their banner and and that's the part of it. So, I think it's going to be it's going to be interesting and it's going to be fun. It's going to be a tough task. So, it'll be something for us to get some extra motivation and and make training camp better about watching the Super Bowl and some guys have said they don't want to go back and rewatch the Super Bowl. Some guys have said, "Yeah, you know, learn from the mistakes, all that." What's your philosophy? >> I think you you definitely take a peek at it. You know, for me, you know, on the biggest stage and a big game and I had a lot of plays I wish I had back. I think you you know, I definitely watched it and um you know, I'm at such a young point in my career where, you know, I can still learn so much and first time playing that defense. So you can learn things and and learn, you know, about the game. So I think there's definitely some parts that you, you know, maybe throws that I maybe skip or, you know, know that now I don't want to watch that again, but there's definitely the game. I think you learn so much from um just, you know, mistakes that you make yourself. >> Drake, is there is there as you enter your second full year under Josh, is there anything specific that you know you don't do as well as you should that you want to work on to create growth in this year? I think as an offense, we're just trying to, you know, keep the ball, you know, you know, moving forward. And I think kind of handling negative plays and and realizing when we keep the ball, you know, ahead of the chains or, you know, in positive plays or just really avoiding negative plays is the biggest thing that, you know, we're working as an offense to, you know, try to, you know, maintain that. And I think we we put some points on the board and we've shown that we can be hard to stop when we do that. And then just like I mentioned, the details, you know, little things of all execution and um inside of each play that go a long way with us, you know, staying ahead of the chains. Some of you guys use a good amount of tempo today. Obviously used it at points last season, but is that something you maybe like to lean more into this season as you're now more comfortable in the offense? >> I think it's tough with the, you know, it makes it tough on the defense. You know, they got to get into calls and sometimes, you know, the defensive coordinator is trying to get the linebacker to make a call and the linebacker may already made a call and it's it's tough on them. It's tough on the guys up front, you know, slows the pass rush down. Um, I think it's an advantage for, you know, any offense, but I think it's tough when you got to bounce, you know, you're running a play fast, but also making it a good play, not just incompletion or something negative. So that's what we're really trying to work on and I think you can only use tempo as much as you know how well you execute and how well how how good you are at it. So working towards that and feeling that out. >> What have you seen from Will Camp going into your uh into his second year? >> Yeah, he will. Um he's got a great mindset. I think he's um kind of understands the business and what this league is about. You know, he kind of got a um a similar experience to me. You know, obviously the seasons that we had were different between mine and his my first year, but you know, he got the full, you know, length of the season, you know, the ups and downs of it. I think he's got a great attitude. Um he's working his butt off in there. Um those offensive linemen, they've been doing a great job in the weight room. Um not lifting the same weights as them, but I've been there with them. So, um it's fun to watch them and I think, you know, he's going to be um he's got a little bit of a, you know, a little extra, you know, motivation for himself to to prove to us and prove to himself he's can be, you know, one of the best players in this league at this position. >> How aware are you of the AJ Brown? You know, how much do you know about him? And, you know, how fun would it be to throw to a guy like that? >> Yeah, I think it's part of the NFL. They throw names around there around every team uh depending whoever looks best in the the graphic and the jersey on social media. So um you know I'm really just focused. We got some new guys in here that I'm working with and um I know that some um you know a lot of talk with that but you know if he ends up being on our team great. You know what a great player and if he doesn't we still got to work these guys here. So it's tough balance but I know he's a phenomenal player. >> How's it going with Romeo Doves? You getting a connection with him or is that still kind of a working? >> I think it's working. I think it's building. I think it's you know he's eager. That's the best thing you see in a in a new receiver and a new offense like Romeo. You know, it's different terminology who's been offense for a couple years with the same quarterback. You know, I kind of got kind of learn, you know, how he likes to do things, how I like to see it when he's running routes and um I think it's just going to be better and better and he's a great player and he's he's got some great he's already been a great player in this league. So, looking forward to, you know, building that connection and, you know, finding his role in this offense. You >> mentioned avoiding negative plays. We saw the interception today. What happened on the play? >> Yeah, just left that route inside. You know, you can't do that in this league. It's as simple as that. So, um, I think, you know, it's part of, you know, throwing out route to the field and and not being, you know, outside with the football. These these players in this league are going to take it the other way. So, um, you know, I think that's that's about it. >> Again, this is, I think, the first time in four or five seasons that you have the same offensive coordinator going from one year to the next. Um, what's it like to be able to kind of have that experience, get to work with Josh and have that continuity run through because again, you haven't had it in a while. >> No, it's it's been awesome. I think not only just going rehashing over last season and how much we learned and how much we kind of bounced ideas off each other, but also just, you know, relearning the little details that he maybe taught me last April or last March that you just kind of, man, okay, if that happens, I remember that and maybe get that. But, you know, I feel like I got a good grasp of it. I guys continue got to, you know, show that I have a good grasp to my teammates on the field and and make good decision and put us in good plays. So that's what I'm working towards, you know, out here in OTAAS and it's pretty much passing camp. So it's it's beautiful for me just to get back there and sling the rock. So it's um it's great work for me and it's awesome to try to take the next steps in this offense. You >> mentioned the bad uh you mentioned the bad taste from the the Super Bowl performance. Have you leaned into that in kind of moving through your offseason? Have you tried to get that out? How have you kind of embraced, you know, that aspect of things in becoming a better version of yourself? >> You know, I think that people always say flush it. I think it's hard to flush, you know, a game like that at that, you know, extent in our sport at the highest level, but at the same time, let it um let you learn from it and let it motivate you and let you, you know, experience what an awesome experience it was. um you know a learning experience and a chance to you know you always wonder what it's like you know I got to um you know I got to feel that and uh didn't play you know we didn't play our best you know as a team and especially myself you know wish I would have played better but u that's something I can you know work on today or work on tomorrow to get back and um just try to get to that that same spot and be on the right side of it >> maybe not a game with the same stakes but Sunday what can we expect >> yeah not the same stakes at all it'll be fun it'll be awesome be a lot of people hopefully Um, we got some fireworks after. Um, I hadn't hit a softball, so hopefully some of the guys on the team will be hitting and hopefully hit some home runs or maybe some strikeouts. So, it should be fun. >> How do you look at this? >> How has May changed with the season you had last year, runner up for the MVP, playing in the Super Bowl. How was it different in May of 2026 from May in 2025 and you? >> Yeah, I think you try not to hopefully have a change. you know, I think you try to have the same um same reasons why you're coming in to work, you know, same reasons why you want to, you know, win football games. And I think that's what the one of the best things we're seeing about this team is we want to, you know, um, you know, get a get back and, you know, kind of not feel like, you know, last year was just a, you know, a one-off year and we're trying to prove ourselves to, you know, to to ourselves, you know, really and and to the to this football um to this football league that we're, you know, tough team to beat. We're going to bring it every day. And I think that's what this identity and what we're building here is starting to become. And I think that takes um it takes a little bit of work, you know, to not just have a a year like we did and and just to, you know, it's hard not to, you know, have a natural falloff or have a natural um get complacent. So, it's going to be uh it's going to be a tough challenge, but at the same time, I think we're up for it and I like the guys and how we've been, you know, working towards that. So, thank you guys.

title: Mike Vrabel: "I'm Going to Be Out There Today in Full Force." | Patriots Press Conference
text: Good to see everybody. >> Jared fund center. >> Hi Mike. >> How are >> you? Any more phones? You guys are >> How are you? >> Great. >> Um as you look to evaluate your group of receivers. Uh well again we always and again and when I say we that includes Elliot and Ryan and Stretch the coaching staff uh we want to continue to improve uh the roster every opportunity that we get and when those opportunities arise I I don't know I know that the guys that we have here are working uh extremely hard. Um young group. I think the oldest person is in there is Jack Driscoll. He's going his seventh year and then uh Brock is going in his sixth I believe. Um, so, you know, it's a good group. They they're very eager to learn. Oh, it's tremendous opportunity. Sure. And they have, you know, they invested a lot of draft capital into it and and all those things are are are are pluses. Um, but they're only pluses on paper if it comes to fruition in my opinion. And so, um, that's our job as line coaches to to, uh, you know, get those players to play at a high level. But, uh, you know, I've also come from, maybe it's old school or not, but really whoever has a helmet out there. I mean, there's a job requirement for the center, the right guard, left, right tackle, and so forth. and whoever fills those roles uh when the gun goes off and we're we're playing, you know, real games. Um whoever's there is there and we have 16 players in that room that are all warrant a chance to to be there. So, um as far as draft status or free agent or how that goes, um fortunately for me, I don't have to concern myself with that. But to answer your question is yes, you have to enhance these draft picks and enhance everyone. James, what have you seen early from Falana that make the transition from right to left? >> Um, he's, you know, he he I saw it when he was in college. I mean, he was a left tackle in college and, um, the thing with him, he just he naturally goes over there and just starts using his left, you know, sets and those kind of things. And that sometimes as coaches, we take that for granted. Um, and I think that, you know, at times we just say, well, just go there and put your left hand down. Well, try riding left-handed if you're right-handed. It's not as easy as you think.
